... And His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And We have certainly struck for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾. We have said that "ḍarb" (striking) is the placing of one thing upon another with force and intensity so that it produces an effect in it. From this comes "ḍarb fi al-ard," meaning to plough it and attend to it so that it yields its produce to you. And "ḍarb al-mathal" (striking a parable) occurs because its outward form is strange. So we say to you: do not find it strange, for it is such-and-such a likeness, and the statement becomes clear and the astonishment goes away. The mathal (parable, likeness) makes the disputed matter resemble the agreed-upon matter.

The root m-th-l occurs in the Noble Qur'an forty-one times in the form "mithl," twenty-two times in the form "mathalan," and three times in the form "mithlahum." His saying, exalted is He: ﴿every kind of example﴾ (min kulli mathal) conveys generality, meaning: We have varied the examples for them in order to explain to them the principles of the religion through what they witness of material things, ﴿so that they may reflect﴾, meaning: that they may contemplate these examples, set each example against its counterpart, and take from the observed a proof of what is hidden, and from the agreed-upon a proof of what is disputed.

Almighty Allah says: "An Arabic Qur'an, without any crookedness, that they may fear Allah" [al-Zumar: 28]. That is: these parables came as an Arabic Qur'an, clear and evident, with no crookedness in it. It is a Book that is read and written, whose recitation is repeated in worship, and it is preserved, not subject to distortion or alteration, for the One who revealed it, He the Glorified, is its guardian. Therefore these parables remain as long as the Qur'an remains, immortal through its immortality. They will remain before you, benefiting from them; whenever the issues of life confront you, you will find the solution to them.

His saying: "without any crookedness" [al-Zumar: 28] means that it does not incline toward any direction, but is upright, for it is the true legislation from Allah, who shows favoritism to no one and flatters no one, not even His messengers. Consider His saying to His Prophet, the best of His messengers, Muhammad (ﷺ): "Then, had We not strengthened you, you would almost have inclined toward them a little. Then We would have made you taste double [punishment] in life and double in death, and you would not have found for yourself any helper against Us" [al-Isra': 74-75].

In Surah al-Kahf the Qur'an is described by His saying: "All praise is due to Allah, who has sent down to His servant the Book and has not made therein any crookedness. [He has made it] straight" [al-Kahf: 1-2].

As for His saying: "that they may fear Allah" [al-Zumar: 28], it means that they may guard against the attributes of majesty of Allah the Exalted and what pertains to them, such as punishment in whatever form of torment.

This is a parable God struck to illustrate the matter of tawhid, clarifying through it the difference between a slave belonging to one master and a slave belonging to several masters. This is an image made up of several elements: the man is owned by partners, and those partners are not in agreement on anything; rather, they are quarrelsome and at odds, each one commanding him to do something. If he pleases this one, he angers that one, and if he obeys one master, he disobeys the other.

So: how can he keep himself from being scattered? And how can he find rest, when he is always bewildered about his affair? As for the other, he is a slave of one master, whose command is one, who is bound to his master, his service devoted to him alone.

﴿Are the two equal in comparison?﴾ [al-Zumar: 29] God leaves it to you to answer this question, ﴿Are the two equal?﴾ [al-Zumar: 29]. We can only say: they are never equal, and we acknowledge this truth ourselves. This is the purpose of the Qur'an, that we acknowledge it ourselves, rather than it being cast to us as a report from God, Exalted is He. And this judgment which we pronounce is affirmed by every intelligent person, and no one rejects it.

So the slave owned by one master is like the one who believed in God, Exalted is He, and sincerely devoted worship to Him alone, while the slave owned by quarrelsome partners is an example of the one who associated others with God in worship. And you, too, should take heed.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Praise be to God﴾ [al-Zumar: 29], meaning: praise be to God for having set forth these parables for us and made matters clear to us, so that we may take the intelligible meaning through the sensible, material image. The one who worships God alone, with no partner, lives with a tranquil mind, a calm soul, and a content heart, unlike the one who worships many gods, who is scattered in soul, unsettled in mind: if he pleases one master he angers the other, and he does not possess the strength that would enable him to please them all.

So praise be to God who sent down the Qur'an in Arabic, without crookedness in it, and praise be to God who set forth in it illustrative parables that bring near to the intellect what it finds difficult to grasp, by means of what all intellects agree upon.

﴿But most of them do not know﴾ [al-Zumar: 29], meaning: they do not know this matter; they do not know that faith in the one true God and sincere servitude to Him, Exalted is He, contains the happiness and rest of the servant, and that servitude to many gods is the wretchedness and exhaustion of the servant.

They do not know this truth because they have not placed the question of faith in lordship under rational examination; rather, they have taken it up just like that, without reflection. What matters to them is that they have a god who has no commands and no prohibitions, a god without a method and without obligations. How good is this god, whom you take according to your mood and in accordance with your desire.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ [al-Zumar: 29], reassures the people of faith and the people of tawhid: though they may be few, they exist, for good is not extinguished no matter how little it is. Among the evidence is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿A multitude of the earlier peoples, and a few of the later ones﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 13-14]. And He said regarding the companions of the right: ﴿A multitude of the earlier peoples, and a multitude of the later ones﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 39-40]. So the good, then, is in this Ummah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 39, verses 30–31:

The disbelievers of Makkah, whenever misfortune or a bout of illness befell the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or hardship struck him, as happened at Uhud, would rejoice at it. So what would they do if the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were to die? Therefore the Qur'an establishes this truth for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, you are to die, and indeed, they are to die﴾ [Az-Zumar: 30]. So why should they rejoice, when this is the end of everyone? As He said in another place: ﴿And We did not grant to any human before you eternity. So if you die, will they be eternal?﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 34].

But the matter will not end at this limit; rather, after death there is another life, in which there is reckoning, recompense, and standing before Allah, the Exalted. At that time the Prophet (ﷺ) will be in the highest station, while as for you, your standing will be the standing of those who opposed Allah. So what will you say? This is the meaning of His, glorified be He, saying: ﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute﴾ [Az-Zumar: 31].

The meaning of ﴿Indeed, you are to die..﴾ [Az-Zumar: 30] is pronounced thus, with the shaddah. That is: going, heading toward death. There is a difference between mayyit with the shaddah on the ya' and mayt with it unvowelled. Mayyit means one who will die and will come to death, even if he is alive, because Allah addressed His Messenger while he was still alive. As for mayt, it is one who has actually died.

From this is the saying of the poet:

Every breath of Allah's creatures among people is mayyit, and the mayt is only one who is carried to the grave.

As for the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, you are to die, and indeed, they are to die﴾ [Az-Zumar: 30], it contains reassurance and consolation for the Messenger of Allah, just as He addressed him saying: ﴿So whether We show you part of what We promise them, or We take you in death, to Us they will return﴾ [Ghafir: 77]. Here He said: ﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute﴾ [Az-Zumar: 31].

That is: either you will see Allah's retribution upon them in this world, or else in the Hereafter. So it is in your interest that you pass on to the Highest Companion, so that the distance is shortened and you see with your own eyes the fate of the stubborn disbelievers, so that you do not weaken or humble yourself, because for you there is a final destination with Allah in which you receive your recompense, and they receive theirs.

When the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, spoke of death in Surah Tabarak, He said: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion, and He is over all things competent. He who created death and life..﴾ [Al-Mulk: 1–2].

Consider His saying ﴿He who created death and life..﴾ [Al-Mulk: 2] and how He placed death first, although it comes after life. That is because life will give you a kind of delusion, when you see your limbs responding to you, the means responding to you, and the world giving to you; delusion must enter you. So the Truth, glorified be He, willed that we not receive life with delusion, but rather receive it first with this truth which contradicts life, namely death.

Therefore: the sensible person understands that he is heading toward death, and he spends the journey of his life while mindful of this end.

As for His saying ﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute﴾ [Az-Zumar: 31]: the first dispute between the prophets and those who disbelieved in them will be over the matter of conveying the message, when the messengers testify that they conveyed Allah's message to their peoples. Then they make excuses, saying: "We thought it was sorcery; we thought it was lies; we thought it was mere imagination." But they did not notice that Allah affirmed this with His saying: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation, that you may be witnesses over the people, and the Messenger will be a witness over you..﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 143].

Therefore: Allah favoured the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ) in that it bore the message of its Messenger, and this is a matter that did not occur with the earlier messengers. For this reason the Exalted said: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind..﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 110]. The proof that the nation bears this message is that no messenger has come after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as though Allah, the Exalted, has entrusted the nation of Muhammad with His message. The Prophet (ﷺ) testified that he conveyed to his nation, and it is upon them to testify that they have conveyed to the people.

This meaning is among the meanings of the wasatiyyah (moderation) of which Allah said: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation..﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 143].

As for its extending to other than that, it is because it is median in everything. We have seen, among other than this nation, those who denied the God, and among them those who affirmed multiple gods; both are extremism. Islam came and taught the worship of one God with no partner, so it chose moderation and balance and resolved this dispute.

Therefore our Lord addressed us saying: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation..﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 143], meaning: within you are aspects of moderation. So if you hear someone speak of communism, or someone speak of capitalism, and if you see someone who is zealous for his school, then say: We are a median nation. We leave to capitalism to yield its ambition, for not everyone has ambition, and when capitalism yields its ambition it must serve society. Look at how many workers work, and how many houses are opened.

Likewise communism: we imposed on them what they did not pay to the one who is not able, so we took the merit of these and the merit of those. The proof is that the two systems that dominated the world for a long period of time began to lessen their ferocity. The capitalists began to ease the intensity of capitalism, looked at the workers, gave them their rights and honoured them, and established unions... etc. And likewise communism: they said that there must exist in society a class able to weigh affairs by their ambitions, and they made for the workers opportunities to work in, and finally communism ended, all praise be to God, entirely.

Therefore: the nation of Islam, the nation of moderation, took the best of both systems.

We say: in the Hereafter there will be the first dispute between the prophets and those who denied them, and a dispute between the leaders of disbelief and those who followed them of the foolish whom they misled and led astray, between the people who influenced the foolish and made them followers of theirs in disbelief.

The Qur'an has depicted this dispute in this setting, saying: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed, and they see the punishment, and ties between them are cut. And those who followed will say, "If only we had a return, so we could disown them as they have disowned us." Thus will Allah show them their deeds as regrets upon them, and they will never leave the Fire.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 166–167].

Therefore the Exalted says: ﴿Intimate friends that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous.﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 67].

Therefore they must now disagree, and some of them curse others, and each one casts the responsibility of following upon the other. Therefore He says: ﴿And stop them, indeed they are to be questioned. What is [the matter] with you that you do not help one another? Rather, they are this Day in surrender. And they will approach one another, questioning each other. They will say, "Indeed, you used to come to us from the right." They will say, "Rather, you were not believers."﴾ [As-Saffat: 24–29].

Thus the follower and the followed dispute, and their group scatters, and they do not help one another as they helped one another in their disbelief in the world.

The Qur'an depicts another situation for the disbelievers, in which their leaders and chiefs went ahead to the Fire, and the followers came and found that the masters had preceded them. The Exalted says: ﴿This, and indeed for the transgressors is an evil destination. Hell, they will burn in it, so wretched is the resting place. This, so let them taste it: boiling water and dark, purulent fluid, and other of its kind in varieties. This is a troop rushing in with you. No welcome for them; indeed, they will burn in the Fire. They will say, "Rather, you—no welcome for you! You put this before us, so wretched is the settlement."﴾ [Sad: 55–60].

That the leaders precede their followers into the Fire indicates that they are greater in crime than those who follow them, because they went astray in themselves and led others astray. It also cuts off the hope of the followers for deliverance and escape from the Fire: who will save them, when they have seen that their masters and leaders went ahead of them into it?

On the other hand, the Truth, glorified be He, presents this dialogue among the believers in Paradise: ﴿A speaker among them will say, "Indeed, I had a companion who used to say, 'Are you really among those who believe? When we die and become dust and bones, will we really be held accountable?'" He will say, "Would you like to look?" So he looks and sees him in the midst of the Blazing Fire.﴾ [As-Saffat: 51–55]. That is: a companion from the people of disbelief.

That is: he looked from the heights and there was his companion in the midst of the Hellfire, meaning in its center. He said: ﴿By Allah, you had almost ruined me. And if not for the favour of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forth.﴾ [As-Saffat: 56–57].

It may also be a dialogue without dispute, as in His saying: ﴿The Day their faces will be turned over in the Fire, they will say, "Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger!" And they will say, "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our elders, and they misled us from the way. Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse."﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 66–68].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 39, verses 30–31:

The disbelievers of Makkah, whenever misfortune or a bout of illness befell the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or hardship struck him, as happened at Uhud, would rejoice at it. So what would they do if the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were to die? Therefore the Qur'an establishes this truth for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, you are to die, and indeed, they are to die﴾ [Az-Zumar: 30]. So why should they rejoice, when this is the end of everyone? As He said in another place: ﴿And We did not grant to any human before you eternity. So if you die, will they be eternal?﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 34].

But the matter will not end at this limit; rather, after death there is another life, in which there is reckoning, recompense, and standing before Allah, the Exalted. At that time the Prophet (ﷺ) will be in the highest station, while as for you, your standing will be the standing of those who opposed Allah. So what will you say? This is the meaning of His, glorified be He, saying: ﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute﴾ [Az-Zumar: 31].

The meaning of ﴿Indeed, you are to die..﴾ [Az-Zumar: 30] is pronounced thus, with the shaddah. That is: going, heading toward death. There is a difference between mayyit with the shaddah on the ya' and mayt with it unvowelled. Mayyit means one who will die and will come to death, even if he is alive, because Allah addressed His Messenger while he was still alive. As for mayt, it is one who has actually died.

From this is the saying of the poet:

Every breath of Allah's creatures among people is mayyit, and the mayt is only one who is carried to the grave.

As for the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, you are to die, and indeed, they are to die﴾ [Az-Zumar: 30], it contains reassurance and consolation for the Messenger of Allah, just as He addressed him saying: ﴿So whether We show you part of what We promise them, or We take you in death, to Us they will return﴾ [Ghafir: 77]. Here He said: ﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute﴾ [Az-Zumar: 31].

That is: either you will see Allah's retribution upon them in this world, or else in the Hereafter. So it is in your interest that you pass on to the Highest Companion, so that the distance is shortened and you see with your own eyes the fate of the stubborn disbelievers, so that you do not weaken or humble yourself, because for you there is a final destination with Allah in which you receive your recompense, and they receive theirs.

When the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, spoke of death in Surah Tabarak, He said: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion, and He is over all things competent. He who created death and life..﴾ [Al-Mulk: 1–2].

Consider His saying ﴿He who created death and life..﴾ [Al-Mulk: 2] and how He placed death first, although it comes after life. That is because life will give you a kind of delusion, when you see your limbs responding to you, the means responding to you, and the world giving to you; delusion must enter you. So the Truth, glorified be He, willed that we not receive life with delusion, but rather receive it first with this truth which contradicts life, namely death.

Therefore: the sensible person understands that he is heading toward death, and he spends the journey of his life while mindful of this end.

As for His saying ﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute﴾ [Az-Zumar: 31]: the first dispute between the prophets and those who disbelieved in them will be over the matter of conveying the message, when the messengers testify that they conveyed Allah's message to their peoples. Then they make excuses, saying: "We thought it was sorcery; we thought it was lies; we thought it was mere imagination." But they did not notice that Allah affirmed this with His saying: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation, that you may be witnesses over the people, and the Messenger will be a witness over you..﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 143].

Therefore: Allah favoured the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ) in that it bore the message of its Messenger, and this is a matter that did not occur with the earlier messengers. For this reason the Exalted said: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind..﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 110]. The proof that the nation bears this message is that no messenger has come after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as though Allah, the Exalted, has entrusted the nation of Muhammad with His message. The Prophet (ﷺ) testified that he conveyed to his nation, and it is upon them to testify that they have conveyed to the people.

This meaning is among the meanings of the wasatiyyah (moderation) of which Allah said: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation..﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 143].

As for its extending to other than that, it is because it is median in everything. We have seen, among other than this nation, those who denied the God, and among them those who affirmed multiple gods; both are extremism. Islam came and taught the worship of one God with no partner, so it chose moderation and balance and resolved this dispute.

Therefore our Lord addressed us saying: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation..﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 143], meaning: within you are aspects of moderation. So if you hear someone speak of communism, or someone speak of capitalism, and if you see someone who is zealous for his school, then say: We are a median nation. We leave to capitalism to yield its ambition, for not everyone has ambition, and when capitalism yields its ambition it must serve society. Look at how many workers work, and how many houses are opened.

Likewise communism: we imposed on them what they did not pay to the one who is not able, so we took the merit of these and the merit of those. The proof is that the two systems that dominated the world for a long period of time began to lessen their ferocity. The capitalists began to ease the intensity of capitalism, looked at the workers, gave them their rights and honoured them, and established unions... etc. And likewise communism: they said that there must exist in society a class able to weigh affairs by their ambitions, and they made for the workers opportunities to work in, and finally communism ended, all praise be to God, entirely.

Therefore: the nation of Islam, the nation of moderation, took the best of both systems.

We say: in the Hereafter there will be the first dispute between the prophets and those who denied them, and a dispute between the leaders of disbelief and those who followed them of the foolish whom they misled and led astray, between the people who influenced the foolish and made them followers of theirs in disbelief.

The Qur'an has depicted this dispute in this setting, saying: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed, and they see the punishment, and ties between them are cut. And those who followed will say, "If only we had a return, so we could disown them as they have disowned us." Thus will Allah show them their deeds as regrets upon them, and they will never leave the Fire.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 166–167].

Therefore the Exalted says: ﴿Intimate friends that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous.﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 67].

Therefore they must now disagree, and some of them curse others, and each one casts the responsibility of following upon the other. Therefore He says: ﴿And stop them, indeed they are to be questioned. What is [the matter] with you that you do not help one another? Rather, they are this Day in surrender. And they will approach one another, questioning each other. They will say, "Indeed, you used to come to us from the right." They will say, "Rather, you were not believers."﴾ [As-Saffat: 24–29].

Thus the follower and the followed dispute, and their group scatters, and they do not help one another as they helped one another in their disbelief in the world.

Interrogation in "﴿Who then is more unjust﴾" [Az-Zumar: 32] carries the sense of wonder and denunciation. That is: no one is more unjust than the one who lies against Allah. Had he lied against other than Allah, it would be abhorrent, so what of one who lies against Allah, to whom nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden, and who knows the realities of things, their secret and their open.

Therefore, lying against Allah is a loss, and if you must lie, then lie against a human like yourself, who is also prone to lying.

For this reason the word ﴿most unjust﴾ came in the form of afʿal (ʾafʿal), which indicates intensification, because the most heinous and greatest injustice is that you lie against Allah. But who is wronged? Is it the one against whom one lies, or is it oneself? Rather, it is oneself that he wrongs.

The matter does not stop there, but ﴿and denied the truth when it came to him﴾ [Az-Zumar: 32], because denying the truth transforms matters into their opposites. A truthful thing is one of which its speaker cannot be told "you lied," because it is a report of events that reality confirms. We have said before: when the verbal relation agrees with the relation of reality, the speech is truthful, and when it contradicts reality, it is false.

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, who is most knowing, asks: ﴿Is there not in Hell a residence for the disbelievers?﴾ [Az-Zumar: 32]. That is: did those who lie against Allah and deny the truth not consider what they think? Did they not know this reality, that Hell is the residence of the disbelieving deniers? Had this reality been in their minds, they would not have dared against Allah. Rather, they are liars, saying what is not the case and not believing in it.

After that, He moves to the one who is distinguished by truthfulness: ﴿And he who brought the truth﴾ [Az-Zumar: 33], who is Muhammad (ﷺ), who received from his Lord and conveyed to his community. Allah, exalted is He, has affirmed the truthfulness of His Messenger in many places, among them: ﴿And if he had made up about Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have severed from him the aorta, and there is none of you who could prevent Us from him﴾ [Al-Haqqah: 44–47].

So the matter of lying against Allah is one in which no one is indulged, not even the messengers. Therefore his (ﷺ) conveyance from his Lord came out precise: you find that he does not convey the meanings of the statements only, but conveys the statements themselves. Read His saying: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ [Al-Ikhlas: 1]. He (ﷺ) could have said to his people: "Allah is One." Thus he would have conveyed the intended meaning of the verse. But he said as it came to him from his Lord: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ [Al-Ikhlas: 1], so he mentioned the command to say ("say").

It is strange that someone should emerge among us who says that such a word be dropped on the pretext that it adds nothing new to the meaning. We say: this is not the speech of a human; rather it is the speech of Allah and His Qur'an, which Allah Himself preserved and conveyed to His Messenger as he received it from his Lord.

Have you seen that if you sent your son to convey a matter on your behalf, and you said to him: "Go to so-and-so and say to him such-and-such," the boy could convey the content of the matter, but when he says: "My father told me, 'Say to so-and-so such-and-such'," this means he affirms the speech and cares for the message as he received it. Therefore, if the word "say" (qul) were dropped, a word of the Qur'an would have been dropped, not an extra word added to it.

As for His saying: ﴿and confirmed it﴾ [Az-Zumar: 33], that is: he confirmed the truth he brought. He himself confirmed it first, and did not wait for us to confirm it or bear witness to it. The Messenger received from his Lord that He is one God with no partner, so he bore witness to that first and affirmed it. Likewise, the Truth, glorified be He, did not wait for the witness of His servants to His oneness, but bore witness to it for Himself first, saying, glorified be He: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge [bear witness]﴾ [Aal-Imran: 18]. After Allah bore witness to His oneness for Himself, it became obligatory upon the Messenger too to bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Thus he brought the truth, confirmed it himself, and said of himself: "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." Likewise the angels bore witness to this oneness, and those of knowledge bore witness to it with the witness of proof, evidence and demonstration.

They said: ﴿And he who brought the truth﴾ [Az-Zumar: 33] is the Messenger of Allah, ﴿and confirmed it﴾ [Az-Zumar: 33], that is: those who confirmed the Messenger of Allah at the beginning of his conveyance from his Lord, whether it was Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) or Lady Khadijah (may Allah be pleased with her). They have differed on this question: is it Abu Bakr or Khadijah? In fact there is no disagreement. If it is said: "the first of the men to believe," we say Abu Bakr; and of the women, Khadijah.

The reality is that Lady Khadijah believed in the Messenger of Allah and confirmed him at the very beginning, perhaps before the news reached Abu Bakr. You know her stance toward the Messenger of Allah when the revelation came to him, and that she took him to her cousin Waraqah ibn Nawfal, who said: "He is the prophet of this community." To confirm this matter for her, he said: "If I live to see your day, I will support you with a mighty support. Would that I were alive the day your people expel you." He said: "Will they expel me?" He said: "No man has ever brought the like of what you have brought except that he was harmed, and you will surely be expelled."

As for the true confirmer (al-Siddiq) Abu Bakr, when they told him that "your companion claims that he is a messenger," he said: "If he said it, then he has spoken the truth." So how did Abu Bakr confirm him when he had not seen from the Messenger of Allah any miracle indicating his messengerhood?

They said: a miracle is not (ʿayyaqa, a stubborn demand) that people believe only through it; rather, miracles are established for those who obstinately resist belief. Therefore the miracle of the Qur'an came as a challenge to the disbelievers and the stubborn deniers. As for one who believed in the Messenger of Allah first, he does not need a miracle. And what miracle made Abu Bakr believe and confirm the Messenger of Allah with such speed?

They said: because he had never found the Messenger of Allah to have lied at all before that. If he was truthful in his affairs with people, would he lie against Allah? Thus Abu Bakr took the miracle from his history with the Messenger of Allah, and likewise Lady Khadijah, as shown by the fact that she was the one who encouraged him, supported him, and said. So the miracle of Muhammad for the first to believe in him was his history and conduct among them.

You know the Prophet's (ﷺ) hadith about Khuzaymah, in which he says: "The quorum of testimony is well known." How then did the Messenger of Allah make Khuzaymah a quorum alone in testimony? And by what did he deserve this rank?

They said: because he excelled decisively in the matter of confirming the Messenger of Allah. The matter is not about the dirhams of a Jew; rather it has another reality. When they wanted to collect the Qur'an, they sought in it the utmost degree of precision, so the compiler would not write a single word in the collected codex unless he saw it written and two witnesses testified to it, to ensure its truth both in memory and in writings. Until he stood before a verse that was written and only one witness testified to it, so he paused. When he saw that this witness was Khuzaymah, he remembered the Messenger's saying about him, and wrote it down.

Among the stances of confirmation was that of the true confirmer Abu Bakr when they told him the news of the Night Journey and the Ascension. They said to him: "Your companion claims that he went to Bayt al-Maqdis and was taken up to heaven in a single night." He did not investigate the matter nor debate it, but at once confirmed and said: "If he said it, then he has spoken the truth." So the scale of truthfulness for him was simply that the Messenger of Allah had said it.

As for His saying: ﴿Those are the righteous (al-muttaqun)﴾ [Az-Zumar: 33], that is: those who took it from its essence, as they say, and placed between themselves and the attributes of majesty of Allah a shield.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 39, verse 34:

His saying: ﴿For them is whatever they wish, with their Lord﴾. That is: all that they wish is available to them in full. But with whom? "With their Lord," at a time when there is no "withness" (ʿindiyyah) except to Allah alone. This "withness" is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To whom belongs the dominion today?﴾ [Ghafir: 16].

So "withness" exists among people in this world: this man is employed by that one, and that one is a servant of this one. But in the Hereafter, "withness" belongs to Allah alone. In this "withness" the believer obtains what he desired in this world and did not obtain in the Hereafter. Allah says: ﴿For them is whatever they wish, with their Lord﴾, and He did not say "for them is whatever they wish," but rather "whatever they wish, with me, Myself." That is: without causes, because causes existed in this world, and what you want through causes may not come to you even if it is in your hand, because Allah exercises His dominion through His vicegerents on earth. So He makes this one a cause for the provision of that one, and that one assists this one, and causes may fail. In the Hereafter, however, there are no causes, but rather the direct giving of Allah without any cause...

If the believer has wishes that are not fulfilled in this world, they are stored up for him in the Hereafter with his Lord. These unfulfilled wishes are covered by one thing: that the noblest wish is that you wish from Allah that He grant victory to His religion, and this wish has been fulfilled.

Therefore: the wish that is not fulfilled is the one that returns to yourself, whereas the wish that conforms to faith in the method of Allah will certainly be fulfilled, as it was fulfilled, for example, at Badr.

So the Truth, glory be to Him, wants of us, when we are believers in Him and affirm His Messenger, that we should have no wish other than for our religion; because a wish outside of religion may be in the hands of people, so they do not fulfil it for you, and perhaps the believer dies before he sees his wish of Allah's victory, so it is stored up for him in the Hereafter.

Therefore: what matters to Him is that the wish be specifically for the victory of Allah's religion over whoever denies and opposes it, and this wish is fulfilled, as the evidence shows: ﴿And indeed Our soldiers, they are the victorious﴾ [al-Saffat: 173].

His saying: ﴿That is the recompense of the good-doers﴾. There is action, and there is grace, and prescribing recompense for action is part of grace. Because when our Lord rewards me for something that returns to me as benefit, this reward is considered an addition. The principle is that He should say to me: "You have already received your recompense as benefit through the deed you did, because your Creator gave you all the causes. He gave you the limbs with which you work, and gave you the earth, the wealth, the air, the water and the food. So if He rewards you for the deed, it is from His grace."

The muhsin (good-doer) has a higher rank than the mu'min (believer). The believer takes what Allah has obligated upon him and carries it out without addition. As for the muhsin, he performs what Allah has obligated upon him and adds to it from the same kind of what Allah has obligated, for example he prays the five prayers and then adds to them whatever he wishes of supererogatory prayers, such as the night prayer. As He, glory be to Him, said of the good-doers: ﴿They used to sleep little of the night, and in the hours before dawn they would seek forgiveness, and in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 17-19].

Here He did not say "a known right" (ḥaqq maʿlūm), because the known right is zakat. But in this station, the servant pays his zakat and then adds to it whatever he wishes of voluntary charity and alms, and these additions your Lord did not demand of you; rather you give them out of love and nearness to Him, glory be to Him.

Therefore: the word ihsan (excellence/good-doing) with Allah has the same meaning as ihsan to people. You say: "I did good (ahsantu) to so-and-so" when you give him more than his right. And when Allah recompenses the good-doer, He gives him the recompense of his excellence; if the servant does good, then Allah is more worthy and more generous.

Allah, glory be to Him, has given us a tangible example of ihsan on earth in what the earth brings forth of its fruits: you place a grain of wheat, for example, and in return it gives you seven hundred grains. If this is the giving of the earth, which was created by Allah, then what of the giving of the Creator, glory be to Him? So the meaning is: ﴿For them is whatever they wish, with their Lord﴾. Why? Because they were good-doers, and this is the recompense of good-doing.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 39, verse 35:

And His saying: ﴿That Allah may remit from them the worst of what they did﴾. This is also from the bounty specific to the degree of ihsan (excellence). The word "worst" (asw'a) indicates intensification, and less than it is "evil" (say'ah). So we have an evil deed and a worse one than it. There is no doubt that "evil" (sayyi'ah) applies to minor sins (saghair), while "the worst" (al-aswa') applies to major sins (kaba'ir). It is as if the one who has entered the station of ihsan has been guaranteed, through the station of ihsan, a kind of settlement that removes his sins, not only the minor ones but the major ones as well. For the One who remits "the worst" remits "the evil" all the more so. This is because you have placed yourself in a station that was not demanded of you, merely out of love for the One who assigned you.

Rather, there is a greater bounty than that: the matter does not end at the remission of sins and evil deeds, but they are changed into good deeds, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ [al-Furqan: 70].

So reflect upon the degrees of bounty from Allah, and the profit in trade with Him, glorified is He.

And with that same honour and grace Allah rewards the doers of ihsan for their good deeds: ﴿and will give them their reward in the best of what they used to do﴾ [al-Zumar: 35]. So just as He forgave them the worst, He rewards them with the best of what they used to do, i.e., with something better than their deeds.

This bounty from Allah, and this generosity and grace from Him toward His servants, encourages the one who has strayed from the call of faith and urges him to return to the fold of faith. There is nothing that stands between him and his Lord, and there is no stumbling block on the path, however many his sins are, as long as the door of repentance is open.

When the Truth, glorified is He, legislated repentance for the disobedient sinners, He legislated it to rescue them from the ferocity of disobedience. For if we said to the disobedient one: "There is no repentance for you," what would he do? [He would despair and persist], meaning: he would despair of reform, persist in corruption and exceed in misguidance. But Allah, glorified is He, does not want that for His servants, so He opened to them the door of repentance to incline them toward the religion of Allah, so that deviation does not increase in society and disobedience does not spread within it.

After the Messenger of Allah informed the people of this divine method of recompense, the obstinate ones said to the Messenger of Allah: "We fear for you, O Muhammad, that our gods may touch you with harm, since you have angered them." Glory be to Allah! They say this while knowing that they are stones that neither harm nor benefit, and when harm touched them, they found no one to turn to but Allah. Therefore the saying of the Exalted was revealed: ﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?﴾...

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 39, verse 36:

It means: O Muhammad, do not concern yourself with this nonsense, for Allah is sufficient for you and suffices you. What shows this is that the believing men used to guard the Messenger of Allah, out of fear that the polytheists would harm him. Then one day they were surprised that the Messenger of Allah dismissed them, ended this guard, and sent it away.

Had the Messenger of Allah not been certain that the One who commanded him to dismiss the guards was sufficient to protect and safeguard him, he would not have done that on his own account. For this reason we have seen the Danish woman, while reading the biography of the Prophet (ﷺ), that he is the greatest of the great who left a clear imprint on history and turned the balance of the world. When she came to this incident and read ﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?﴾ [az-Zumar: 36], and read ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67], she said: "By God, Muhammad did not do that except while certain of his Lord's protection of him. Even if he deceived all the people, he did not deceive himself," and she believed because of this matter.

His saying, glorified is He: ﴿أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِكَافٍ عَبْدَهُ﴾ ("Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?"). Some like to say the meaning is: "Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?", and they regard the bāʼ (ب) as superfluous (zāʼida). This is not correct, for there is no superfluous particle in the speech of Allah, the Exalted. Here the hamzah is an interrogative of denial (istifhām inkārī), and denial implies negation; what follows it is not a negation, and the negation of a negation is an affirmation.

That is: we deny that Allah is not sufficient for His servant, and since we deny that Allah is not sufficient for His servant, the result is that Allah, the Exalted, is sufficient for His servant.

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has a name, which is Allah, and has attributes, which we know through the Most Beautiful Names. Among His Most Beautiful Names is al-Kafi (the All-Sufficient). The meaning, then, is: "Is not Allah described as the One who suffices His servant?" So how can we then say that the bāʼ is superfluous?

To say that the bāʼ is superfluous here contradicts the eloquence of the Qur'an, and we should not say that there is a superfluous letter in the Qur'an. Some, showing courtesy toward the words of Allah, say: "Rather, it is a particle of connection (ḥarf ṣila)," and others say: "a particle linking existence (ḥarf li-rabṭ al-wujūd)." We have no need of all these interpretations...

As for those who said the bāʼ in bi-kāfin is superfluous, they regarded (laysa) as one of the "sisters of kāna" (akhawāt kāna), which raises the subject and puts the predicate in the accusative. So the word Allah is its subject in the nominative, and kāfin is its predicate, and the estimate is: "Is not Allah sufficient His servant?" This contradicts the majesty and eloquence of the Qur'an.

As for His saying: ﴿وَيُخَوِّفُونَكَ بِالَّذِينَ مِن دُونِهِ﴾ ("and they threaten you with those other than Him"), that is: with the idols. ﴿وَمَن يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُ مِنْ هَادٍ﴾ ("And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide"), meaning: leave them to say what they say, for Allah has led them astray, so who will guide them?

This is what al-Sha'rawi says about surah 39, verse 37:

Meaning: O Muhammad, do not be concerned with this nonsense, for God is sufficient for you and will protect you. The proof of this is that the believing men used to guard the Messenger of God out of fear that the polytheists would harm him. Then one day they were surprised that the Messenger of God dismissed them, ended this guard, and sent them away.

Had the Messenger of God not been certain that the One who ordered him to dismiss the guards would protect and defend him, he would not have done this on his own. This is why we saw the Danish woman, while she was reading his biography (ﷺ), learning that he was one of the greatest figures who left a clear mark on history and turned the scales of the world. When she reached this incident and read ﴿Is not God sufficient for His servant?﴾ [az-Zumar: 36] and read ﴿And God will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67], she said: "By God, Muhammad did not do this except because he was certain of his Lord's protection of him. Had he deceived all the people, he would not have deceived himself." And she believed because of this matter.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Is not God sufficient for His servant?﴾ [az-Zumar: 36], some like to say the meaning is: "Is not God sufficient for His servant?", and they regard the particle bi (ب) as superfluous (zā'id). This is not correct, for there is no superfluous particle in the speech of God, the Exalted. Here the hamzah is an interrogative of denial (istifhām inkārī), and denial implies negation, and after it the negation of a negation is an affirmation.

That is: we deny that God is not sufficient for His servant. And since we deny that God is not sufficient for His servant, the result is that God, the Exalted, is sufficient for His servant.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, has a name, which is Allah, and He has attributes, which we know through the Most Beautiful Names. Among His Most Beautiful Names is al-Kafi (the Sufficient). The meaning, then, is: "Is not God described as being sufficient for His servant?" So how then can we say that the bi is superfluous?

To say that the bi is superfluous here contradicts the eloquence of the Qur'an, and we should not say that there is a superfluous letter in the Qur'an. Some are polite with the words of God and say: "Rather, it is a particle of connection (harf ṣilah)," and others say: "A particle linking existence (harf li-rabṭ al-wujūd)." But we have no need for all these interpretations.

We explained this matter earlier. If we say, for example, "Mā 'indī māl" (I have no money), the "mā" here negates the existence of money that is considered worthwhile, and does not preclude that I may have a pound or two pounds, for example. But if you say, "Mā 'indī min māl," meaning: from the very beginning of what is called money, not even a single millim, then the preposition here is not superfluous in the speech; rather, it is foundational in meaning.

As for those who said that the bi in ﴿bi-kāfin﴾ [az-Zumar: 36] is superfluous, they regarded laysa as one of the sisters of kāna (akhawāt kāna), which raise the subject and put the predicate in the accusative. So the word of majesty (Allah) is its subject in the nominative, and kāfin is its predicate. The implied construction becomes: "Is not God sufficient His servant?" and this contradicts the majesty and eloquence of the Qur'an.

As for His saying: ﴿And they threaten you with those besides Him﴾ [az-Zumar: 36], that is, with the idols; ﴿and whomever God leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾ [az-Zumar: 36], meaning: leave them to say what they say, for God has led them astray, so who will guide them? ﴿And whomever God guides, for him there is no misleader﴾ [az-Zumar: 37]. This is the counterpart: if God guides us to the path, no one will lead us astray. ﴿Is not God Mighty, Possessor of Retribution?﴾ [az-Zumar: 37], meaning: is not God described as being Mighty? So the bi here is like the preceding one.

Al-'Azīz is the one who overcomes and is not overcome. Since He, glorified is He, is overpowering and cannot be overcome, beware of His retribution, for He is ﴿Possessor of Retribution﴾ [az-Zumar: 37]. However much you devise with corrupt thinking, plotting and conspiring, you will not overcome Him.

It is astonishing that the disbelievers threaten the Messenger of God with idols, while they know their reality and their own statement about them: ﴿We worship them only that they may bring us nearer to God in position﴾ [az-Zumar: 3]. This statement is linguistically false, because worship (ʿibādah) is the worshipper's obedience to the worshipped in its commands and prohibitions. And what command or prohibition do the idols issue? So this statement of theirs is nonsense and falsehood.

For this reason, when God softened the heart of our master Khalid ibn al-Walid for Islam, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) wished to send him to demolish al-'Uzza. When Khalid went to it and took his axe to break it, he said to it:

O Uzza, disbelief in you, not glorification!
Indeed I have seen that God has humiliated you.

Had this been a god, it would have frightened him and prevented itself.

Some orientalists paused at this verse, ﴿And they threaten you with those besides Him﴾ [az-Zumar: 36], that is, with the idols, and they said: The idols al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat are all feminine names, so how does the Qur'an say "alladhīna" (those, masculine) and not "allātī" (those, feminine)? We say: there is a difference between the name of an idol and its referent. That is, its name is "idol" (ṣanam), and this idol was named al-Lat or al-'Uzza. So insofar as it is an idol, the plural is masculine; insofar as it is the named entity, it is feminine. Thus alladhīna refers to the name, that is, to the idols, and allātī refers to the named.

We pause here at this contrast in His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And whomever God leaves astray, for him there is no guide. And whomever God guides, for him there is no misleader. Is not God Mighty, Possessor of Retribution?﴾ [az-Zumar: 36-37]. The one who is astray (ḍāll) is the one who does not find his way to his goal, like one who has lost the road and does not know where to go. This one is astray unintentionally, since he does not know.

The word ḍāll also comes with the meaning of bewildered and perplexed, as in His saying, addressing His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And He found you lost and guided you﴾ [ad-Duha: 7], because the Prophet saw his community doing things that did not please him, while he still did not know the correct course of action to take, that is, he did not know the truth, not that he knew it and turned away from it. There is a difference between the two states. So straying here is not intended.

Ḍalāl also comes with the meaning of forgetting, as in His saying: ﴿So that if one of them errs, the other will remind her﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282].

Among straying is forgetting the ancient primordial covenant that God took from us in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes"﴾ [al-A'raf: 172].

The opposite of straying is guidance (hidāyah), which also comes with various meanings. But those who twist the words of God and want to object to them take it in one meaning only and apply it to all its subjects, but this is not correct.

Guidance is applied to absolute indication (dalālah muṭlaqah), meaning that someone points you the way and you are free to obey him or turn away from him. We gave an example of this: the traffic policeman who directs you and shows you the road, after which you are free to take the road or not. If you take the road he showed you and thank him for his favour, saying: "May God increase your goodness; had it not been for you, I would have lost the way," he then looks at you differently and sees you as deserving of more good. He says to you: "By God, you are a good man, and I will go with you until you pass this area, because there are dangers in it." This is called assistance (maʿūnah). So whoever believes in the One who guided and indicated is worthy of being assisted and granted success for more guidance.

This is the meaning of God's saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad: 17], meaning: He increases them through His assistance, eases the hardships of obedience for them, and turns away the causes of evil from them. So the first is the guidance of absolute indication, and the second is the guidance of assistance and granting success.

The Truth, glorified is He, clarified these two guidances in His address to His Prophet (ﷺ). He said of the first: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [ash-Shura: 52], and He said of the second: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but God guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Qasas: 56]. How, then, can guidance be affirmed for the Messenger of God in one verse and negated in another, when the matter is one and the agent is one?

They said: Because the aspect is distinct. The guidance that is negated is other than the guidance that is affirmed. The Truth says to His Prophet Muhammad: You are only a conveyer, a guide and an indicator; you are not the one who lays down the methods, and you have no power to compel people to believe. Your duty is only to convey, because your conveying is God's guidance for people. But it is not your task to put faith into hearts.

Similar to this is His saying, the Exalted, in one verse: ﴿...But most of the people do not know. They know an outward appearance of the worldly life...﴾ [ar-Rum: 6-7].

Thus He affirmed knowledge for them and negated it from them in the same verse. Why? Because the aspect is distinct. The knowledge that is negated is other than the knowledge that is affirmed.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whomever God leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾ [az-Zumar: 36], "God leaves astray" means He attributes straying to him, saying: "This one is astray," meaning he has left the path that He has laid out for him. The one whom God has judged as astray cannot be described by any person of sound mind as rightly guided, because when he opposes what God requires of him and what he does, natural reason concludes that he is astray and not guided.

For example, the Truth said to us: "Be truthful in your speech," and He forbade us from lying. What does a sensible person say when he compares truthfulness and lying? He must say: "Truthfulness is guidance, and lying is straying," and he cannot say otherwise, especially if he puts the matter to himself: Would you like people to be truthful with you, or to lie to you?

So whoever God leaves astray and judges to be astray after the path has been shown to him, no one can describe him as rightly guided, because God's guidance is a matter on which all natural minds agree, especially when you yourself feel the consequence of this straying and are burned by its fire.

For this reason you find that the liar loves the truthful, and the wicked loves the good and noble. As an example of this, we took three young men, teenagers who walked through life with their hair loose ("ḥall shaʿrihim"), following the idle path. One of them repented and God accepted him, and he withdrew from them. They began to mock him and call him names like "the bucket" and "the lock," and so on. Then one of the other two wanted to marry off his sister. To whom would he give her: to his companion who agreed with him in evil and corruption, or to the other one who repented and withdrew from their evil? So: falsehood may tempt you, but in the end truth must prevail, must appear and must rise. ﴿Is not God Mighty, Possessor of Retribution?﴾ [az-Zumar: 37]. So be patient on its path.

The Lord, glory be to Him, wished to expose the folly of their reasoning in worshipping idols. He also wished to establish against them the proof and argument of the invalidity of this worship, and for this proof to be an acknowledgment from them, not a statement from Him, glory be to Him. We have said: establishing a ruling is either by a statement from you or by an acknowledgment from the other party. And acknowledgment, as we have said, is the master of proofs. You do not leave it to the addressee to judge himself unless you are confident that he will say what you want, as you say to one who denies your favour: "Did I not do good to you on such-and-such a day?" You only say it when you are sure he cannot deny it.

Therefore, the Lord, glory be to Him, asks them here about the greatest thing in creation, or the highest container that holds all creatures, which is the heavens and the earth. Man was created with the universe already in existence before he was created; he arrived upon an earth in which there are crops, plants, water, air and good soil, and upon a sky in which there are planets, stars, the sun and the moon.

So He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And if you ask them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they will surely say, "God."﴾ [al-Zumar: 38]. They must say "God", and God alone, because they turned their thinking over and found no one who claimed this creation, and it did not occur to any of the unbelievers, the obstinate, or those who deny the existence of God that he could make this claim.

If we trace the creation of man from Adam, peace be upon him, and those who came from his offspring, we find that he arrived upon this universe with its heavens and its earth. So if we asked him, "Did you create the heavens and the earth?" he could not say, "I created them."

So ask them, O Muhammad, this question: ﴿Who created the heavens and the earth?﴾ [al-Zumar: 38], and they must say "God", because no period has passed in which an existent had no earth and heaven in its existence, so that it could be said that it brought them into being when it came; rather, everyone is a newcomer to this universe.

Similarly: ﴿And if you ask them, "Who created them?" they will surely say, "God."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 87], because the first creature created and brought into being cannot be told by anyone, "I created you," nor can he himself say, "I created myself."

Their answer here, "God", draws our attention to another matter: the word "God" revolves on their tongues and they understand its meaning, otherwise they would not utter it. This is because meanings exist first, and then words are assigned to signify them. We gave as an example the "television": before it existed we did not know this name, but when it came into being we gave it the name. So then: how did the word "Allah" enter people's language?

Thus, the word of majesty "Allah" has its meaning, and He, the Truth, glory be to Him, existed before this word existed. Therefore we say to whoever denies the existence of God, the Exalted: your speech is self-contradictory, for your saying "God does not exist" is not coherent, because "God" is the subject about which a judgment is made, and "does not exist" is the predicate that is judged. How, then, do you say He does not exist, when the meaning exists before its word?

The word "Allah" has come into a language only because He, glory be to Him, exists, existing before the name, and we knew the name only because its Owner informed us of it. For the work of reason in faith is to indicate to you that behind this universe there is a Creator who brought it into being; but what is this power, and what does He want from creation? This is not the task of reason. Reason does not reach it; we know it only through the message from this Creator.

You remember that we gave an example of this matter: we are sitting in a house, and then the doorbell rings. At the moment we hear the bell, we all agree that someone is at the door, because every event must have a cause. But who is he? What does he want? We do not know unless he himself informs us of his identity and says, "I am so-and-so, and I want such-and-such."

So, reason with respect to the Supreme Existence does not perceive the particulars of the Supreme Existence; it only believes in its existence and infers it. He, glory be to Him, informs us of His name, His attributes, His method and His requirements, for the message must come from the one who holds the matter.

And among the failures of the philosophers in inquiry is that they wanted to introduce reason not only into the intelligible but into the conception of the intelligible, and conception is not their task, because you cannot conceive the form of this intelligible; you only comprehend the existent and then leave existence to speak about itself...

So the Lord, glory be to Him, said and informed that He is the One who created this creation; this existence does not exist unless a finder has found it, and I am the One who brought it into being. No opposing claim has stood against this assertion, so the claim is established for its owner until an opponent appears.

Therefore we have already said: the word "kufr" (disbelief) is itself evidence of faith, because "kufr" means concealment, and only something existent can be concealed. Thus disbelief is an accident upon faith, as if the original state of the sound nature is faith, then disbelief arose upon it to conceal it.

After they said "God" and acknowledged the first argument, that He, glory be to Him, is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, He said to them: ﴿Say: "Have you considered what you call upon besides God?"﴾ [al-Zumar: 38], meaning: inform me. He thus gave them leave, so that they would say and inform about those they call upon besides God, namely the idols: ﴿If God intends harm for me, are they removers of His harm?﴾ [al-Zumar: 38], that is, are the idols ﴿removers of His harm﴾ [al-Zumar: 38]? The answer can only be negative, because the idols first do not hear the supplication of one who supplicates to them, nor do they perceive his request, so how could they respond to him by removing harm from him?

On the other side: ﴿Or if He intends mercy for me, are they withholders of His mercy?﴾ [al-Zumar: 38]. The answer is likewise negative. Thus, benefit is established for God by their own acknowledgment, and the invalidity is established for their gods. But if they falter after that and do not answer you, because the answer would bind them to the argument, then say: ﴿God is sufficient for me﴾ [al-Zumar: 38], meaning: in bringing about benefit in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and God is sufficient for me in removing harm from me; He suffices me.

This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He, in the preceding verse: ﴿Is not God sufficient for His servant?﴾ [al-Zumar: 36]. "Sufficient for him" means: He gives him favour: first the favour of existence, then the favour of the continuation of this existence and the preservation of life, then the favour of preserving the species. After that He removes from him the harm that befalls him and descends upon him. When harm touches a person in himself, he never turns to a false god, because he does not deceive himself or lie to himself. Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Those whom you call upon vanish except Him﴾ [al-Isra: 67].

His saying: ﴿In Him do the reliant put their trust﴾ [al-Zumar: 38] here is a form of restriction (qasr), restricting reliance to God alone, and this is true reliance. For one who relies upon something makes for its strength a reserve, which fails when that strength is gone. Therefore the wise person is the one who relies upon the One who aids him and helps him, and when he needs Him, finds Him. We have said: whoever relies upon the like of himself is a loser, for you rely on him, you expect him to meet your needs, and after days you read his obituary in the newspapers. Therefore our Lord, glory be to Him, teaches us how to rely, saying: ﴿And rely upon the Living who does not die﴾ [al-Furqan: 58].

There is a difference between tawakkul (reliance) and tawakul (negligent dependence). For God's hand has long been extended to creation through means: the means of preserving life through food and drink, and the means of preserving the species through marriage.

When the Lord, glory be to Him, guaranteed us these means, He gave us a role in them. The earth, for example, is before you, the sun shines upon it, the wind blows over it, and rain waters it; and it is incumbent upon you to make use of these means by plowing the land, sowing the seeds and tending them, so that the earth gives you its produce. Do not expect to sit in your house while the means bring you food and place it on your table, because your Lord created you and created for you the limbs, and made them responsive to your will: your hand can strike with it, and it can wipe the head of an orphan with it; your tongue can utter with it the word of monotheism, and it can utter with it what contradicts it.

But remember that your limbs are subject to your will only in this world; as for the Hereafter, you have no authority over them, for they will be under the authority of their Creator, on the day when He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿"To whom belongs dominion this Day?"﴾ [Ghafir: 16]. Then your limbs will be freed from your authority and will bear witness against you: ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will bear witness against them concerning what they used to do﴾ [al-Nur: 24].

These means and these limbs which God created for you, He did not create them for you to render them idle. So if the work is within your capacity and you ask someone else to do it, this is negligent dependence: to neglect God's means and be heedless of this kingdom which God made subject to you and obedient to you, which carries out your command merely by your will. This is a dignity God has granted you in your own self; so how would you humble yourself by relying upon the like of you? And how would you refuse God's hand extended to you?

So if you take the means, and employ your mind and your limbs in what God has given you, then you are a reliant. The reality of tawakkul is that you work with your limbs and rely upon God with your heart, and expect that trial may befall you, so you work and take the means, and they do not give you (what you hoped), like one who plants a field and a calamity comes and destroys the crop, for example.

Reflect on this address. After their obstinacy, their insistence on falsehood, and their refusal to accept the proofs and evidence, the Exalted still shows tenderness toward them. He commands His Messenger ﷺ to address them with this affectionate call: "O my people" (يا قوم). It means: I am not a stranger to you; you are my family and my tribe among whom I live.

When the Messenger of God called them and they did not respond, and the proofs demonstrating the falsehood of their worship of idols did not prevail with them, his Lord commanded him to say to them: ﴿O my people, act according to your standing; indeed I am acting﴾ (Az-Zumar 39:39). The meaning of "act according to your standing" is like saying to someone who does not respond to you: "Do whatever you wish."

The meaning, then, is: act according to your standing. That is: bring all your capabilities against me. Why? Because he relies upon his Lord, and his Lord is sufficient for him. He does not say this recklessly or out of arrogance; he says it on the basis of the Almighty's words: ﴿Is not God sufficient for His servant?﴾ (Az-Zumar 39:36).

The word مَكَانَتِكُم (makanatikum, "your standing") in Az-Zumar 39:39 has two forms here: makan (place) and makanah (standing). The makan is the space occupied by a thing. The makin is the one who occupies a place. For example, a cup is a makan, and the water in it is makin. You yourself have a place you occupy, and even if someone oppresses you and expels you from it, he must send you to another place.

If this place expands for you, and you come to have authority over a wider place in which you hold power, command, and prohibition, then this is makanah. It is said of one whose influence and authority have grown: "He has makanah." The added ta' here is what they call the ta' of intensification (taʾ al-mubālaghah)...

So: makanah is what you have authority and governance over, which helps you attain your aim.

His saying ﴿indeed I am acting﴾ means: you act according to your standing and your capacity in obstinacy, oppression, and harm; and I act according to my standing in the call, in giving you counsel, and in eagerness for your guidance. This is my mission, and I will not abandon it. I will persist in spreading it and bear your persecution of me and my companions, and nothing will turn me away from my aim.

His saying ﴿so you will know﴾ (Az-Zumar 39:39): what is known here is ﴿who will receive a punishment that disgraces him﴾ (Az-Zumar 39:40), that is, in this world, ﴿and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment﴾ (Az-Zumar 39:40), that is, in the Hereafter. Reflect here on the word سوف (sawfa, "will"), which denotes the future. It did not say "now," because Islam began as something strange, and it spread first among the weak and the slaves, who were persecuted, killed, harmed, and expelled from their homes and their wealth in the cause of the call to truth.

The Exalted wished to test the people of faith who bear this call, to distinguish from among them those weak in conviction, and to remove from them the people of frailty and hypocrisy who are unfit to carry this message. Therefore, the revelation came down to the Messenger of God from time to time with a weighty command, and each time such a command descended, some of them were eliminated, until none remained around the Messenger of God except the sound of faith, the strong in conviction.

In this verse there is also a threat from the Messenger of God to the deniers, concerning events that are yet to come. This threat is evidence of his ﷺ confidence that the One who revealed this threat to him is able to bring it about as He announced it; otherwise the Messenger of God would not have said it, since time will reveal the truth or falsehood of this threat...

We have said that the truthfulness of the Messenger concerning matters related to his community is one thing, and his truthfulness concerning matters related to himself is another. His truthfulness concerning matters related to himself is more emphatic. We mentioned the story of the woman who embraced Islam when she read the interpretation of the Exalted's words to His Messenger: ﴿And God will protect you from the people﴾ (Al-Ma'idah 5:67). When his Lord gave him assurance that he would not be assassinated by people, the Messenger ﷺ dismissed his guards and did not keep them, despite this promise. This woman paused in an intellectual stance and said: "If he had deceived all the people, he would not have deceived himself." So this is the Messenger's confidence in God's promise.

As for the Exalted's words ﴿so you will know﴾ rather than "you will see" or "you will observe": knowledge is broader and more general than sight. The events that will come may be far from their sight, occurring in other places that some see and some do not see; but knowledge conveys to you what your senses perceive and what the senses of others perceive.

So, by knowledge you take in the knowledge of others. When you see and reason, you are guided to a judgment through the conception of reason; and through knowledge you benefit from what others have reasoned. Thus knowledge has a wider scope than the data of reason and the senses.

His saying ﴿and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment﴾ (Az-Zumar 39:40): the word muqim (lasting) came to respond to a statement they themselves had made earlier, because their wars used to continue for a long time, up to forty years, and would be between them in alternation, a day for you and a day against you. So they may have supposed that punishment is likewise a period that comes to an end. Therefore He wished to affirm to them that when punishment descends upon them, there will be no alternation like the alternation of war; rather, it is lasting and permanent.

Here is the call: ﴿O my people﴾ [Az-Zumar: 39]. After their obstinacy, their persistence in falsehood, and their refusal to accept the proofs and evidence, Allah, glorified is He, still shows compassion towards them. So He commands His Messenger (ﷺ) to address them with this tender call: (O my people). That is, I am not a stranger to you; you are my family and my tribe, among whom I live.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called them and they did not respond, and the proofs and evidence that demonstrate the falsehood of their worship of idols did not succeed with them, his Lord commanded him to say to them: ﴿O my people, act according to your position; indeed I am acting...﴾ [Az-Zumar: 39]. The meaning is: act according to your position, just as you say to someone who has not responded to you: "Do whatever you wish." Or (ride whatever horse you have).

So the meaning is: act according to your position. That is, take all your capabilities against me. Why? Because he relies upon his Lord, and He is sufficient for him. He does not say this recklessly or arrogantly, but says it on the basis of the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?﴾ [Az-Zumar: 36].

The word ﴿مَكَانَتِكُـمْ﴾ [Az-Zumar: 39] (makanatikum) has two forms for us: makan and makana. The makan is the space that a thing occupies. The makin is the one who occupies a place. So a cup, for example, is a makan and the water in it is makin. You yourself have a place that you occupy, so even if someone oppresses you and expels you from it, he must send you to another place.

If this place expands for you and you come to have authority over a place wider than it, in which you have power, command and prohibition, this is makana (position, standing). So it is said of one whose status and authority have grown: he has makana. The extra ta' here is called the ta' of intensification (ta' al-mubalagha), as we say of intensification in knowledge: ʿālim, ʿallām and ʿallāma. The word ʿallāma is the peak of knowledge, said of one who has reached a level in his field such that nothing of it is hidden from him.

If you say: why did Allah describe Himself, glorified is He, as ʿallām, and not as ʿallāma? We say: because the knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, admits of no gradation; there is nothing in it of partial and total, so Allah, glorified is He, is not described by this attribute.

From makana is His saying, the Exalted, in the story of our master Joseph, peace be upon him: ﴿And thus We established Joseph in the land, to settle therein wherever he willed﴾ [Yusuf: 56]. That is: We did not give him a mere place; rather We gave him makana and a wide authority by which he moves here and there wherever he wills. A person may have a place, then a force comes that establishes him in it, as in the story of our master Joseph, peace be upon him. And he may have a place, then a force comes and removes him from it, as it did to me when it took me and threw me into a cell.

We have already said that in the language there is a hamza called the hamzat al-izala (the hamza of removal): when it enters a verb it removes what the verb describes. As you say: aʿjama al-kalam, meaning: he removed its obscurity and clarified its meaning. From this is the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his supplication to his Lord: [...]. That is: if something has occurred from him that angers You, then I remove Your reproach of me until I reach Your pleasure with me. We say: ʿatiba fulān ʿalā fulān fa-aʿtabahu, meaning: he removed his reproach by apologizing to him or reconciling with him, because ʿatb is blame for something that should not occur between loving ones. From this is His saying, the Exalted, in the word we have here (makana): ﴿And if they intend to betray you, they have already betrayed Allah before, so He gave you power over them. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ [Al-Anfal: 71].

So the meaning of (fa-amkana minhum) is: He removed their place. And we say: fulān tamakkana min fulān, meaning: he was able over him and removed him from his place or his position.

Thus, the word makana is that over which you have authority and guardianship that enables you to achieve your aim. So makan, when you intensify it, becomes makana, and the ta' is for intensification. It also comes for prestige that extends over what does not enter your possession in terms of disposal, but enters your possession as awe. Therefore, when Malik was killed, they said: "Malik used to protect the places of the clouds." That is, wherever a cloud passed and rained, its rain was protected by Malik, so that no one would encroach upon it. This was only because of his standing among the people, so he protected the places of the clouds outside his own land.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed I am acting﴾ [Az-Zumar: 39], it means: you, act according to your position and capacity in obstinacy, persecution and harm, and I act according to my position in the call, in advising you, and in eagerness for your guidance. This is my message and I will not abandon it. I will exert effort in spreading it and bear your persecution of me and of my companions. Nothing will turn me away from my aim.

As for His saying: ﴿then you will know﴾ [Az-Zumar: 39], what is known here is: ﴿on whom will come a punishment that will disgrace him﴾ [Az-Zumar: 40], that is, in this world, ﴿and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment﴾ [Az-Zumar: 40], that is, in the Hereafter. Consider here the word sawfa, which indicates the future. He did not say "now," because Islam began as something strange and spread first among the weak and the slaves, who were persecuted, killed, harmed, and expelled from their homes and their wealth in the cause of the call to truth.

Allah, glorified is He, wanted to purify the believers who carry this call, and to distinguish from among them those weak in faith, and to remove from them the people of weakness and hypocrisy who are not fit to carry this message. Therefore the revelation used to descend upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a noble command at every period, and each time such a command descended some of them were eliminated, until none remained around the Messenger of Allah except the sound in faith, strong in conviction.

In this verse there is also a threat from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the deniers, concerning events that will come. This threat is evidence of his (ﷺ) confidence that the one who revealed this threat to him is able to bring it about as he announced it; otherwise the Messenger of Allah would not have said it, because time will reveal whether this threat is true or not.

The same applies to a promise that the Messenger of Allah announces before its time. Read, for example, this promise: ﴿The multitude will be routed and they will turn their backs﴾ [Al-Qamar: 45]. This is a promise from Allah to the believers, revealed in the most severe and dire circumstances, when they were persecuted and unable to protect themselves.
