Therefore, when this verse was revealed, ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "What multitude is this, when we are unable to protect ourselves?" But when he saw it at Badr he said: "My Lord has spoken truly, and His Messenger has spoken truly." This promise does not cast doubt on the call; rather it aims to confirm it. So there is truthfulness in promise and truthfulness in threat.

We have said that the Messenger's truthfulness in matters concerning his community is one thing, and his truthfulness in matters concerning himself is another. His truthfulness in matters concerning himself is more emphatic. We also mentioned the story of the woman who embraced Islam when she read the interpretation of His saying to His Messenger: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 67]. When his Lord gave him assurance that he would not be assassinated by the people, he (ﷺ) dismissed his guards and did not keep them, relying on this promise. This woman paused and reflected, and said: "If he deceived all the people, he would not have deceived himself." So this is the Messenger's trust in the promise of Allah.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿then you will know﴾ [Az-Zumar: 39], He did not say "you will see" or "you will look," because knowledge is broader and more comprehensive than sight. The events that will come may be far from their view, occurring in other places, seen by some and not seen by others. But knowledge conveys to you what your senses perceive and what the senses of others perceive.

So through knowledge you acquire the knowledge of others. When you see and reason, you are guided to judgment through the conception of reason, and through knowledge you benefit from what others have understood. Thus knowledge has a wider scope than the data of reason and the senses.

As for His saying: ﴿and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment﴾ [Az-Zumar: 40], the word muqim (lasting) came to respond to something they themselves had said. Wars among them used to continue for a long time, up to forty years, and were alternating between them, a day for you and a day against you. So they may have thought that the punishment would be similar, lasting for a period and then ending. Therefore He wanted to emphasize to them that when punishment descends upon them, there is no alternation in it like the alternation of war; rather it is lasting and permanent.

We notice that Almighty Allah sometimes speaks of His Essence with the plural pronoun (*innā*, "We") and sometimes with the singular (*innī* or *innanī*, "I"). When the subject is tawhid (the Oneness of God), He uses the singular, as in His words to our master Musa: ﴿Indeed, I am Allah﴾ [Ta-Ha: 14], because He wants to establish the matter of tawhid and affirm that He is one God with no partner. When the subject concerns a matter in which He acts and His vicegerents on earth also act, the plural is used, as here: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for mankind﴾ [al-Zumar: 41].

Consider the prepositions in *ʿalayka* ("upon you") and *lil-nās* ("for mankind"). Prepositions in the language have wide meanings. *ʿalayka* indicates that I am placing responsibility upon you, whereas the *lām* in *lil-nās* indicates benefit for them. As we say in accounts: *lahu* ("for him") gives benefit, and *ʿalayhi* ("against him") gives obligations.

It is as if Almighty Allah is saying: O people, O you who listen to the call of Muhammad, know that it is for your own good, and it returns to you with benefit and gain. We have sent down to him a heavy burden that will weary him in his person and in his family, and will expose him to mockery, harm, and conspiracy, and so on.

So the Book was sent down to you, O Muhammad, with its obligations and responsibilities. Bear it, and be among the *ulū al-ʿazm* (the possessors of resolve) from the messengers who came before you. Although they occupied a limited space in time and place, you have occupied a space that is not limited, neither in time nor in place. When you bear the hardships in the way of your call, know that you will bear hardships in proportion to the universality of your message.

Therefore, the good of the call of Islam is for you, and its hardships are borne by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This is the meaning of ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for mankind﴾ [al-Zumar: 41], i.e., for their benefit.

When we expand on the particles and stand on their meanings, we take as an example His words at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿They are upon guidance from their Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 5].

The believers are upon guidance, and *ʿalā* ("upon") indicates elevation, as if guidance is a mount that carries them and gives them rest; it does not tire them, and it delivers them to their goal. In this way guidance came to relieve people and carry them to the noblest ends. So hold fast to it, for it did not come to load you with what you cannot bear; it came to serve you.

As for His words ﴿with the truth﴾ [al-Zumar: 41]: *al-ḥaqq* (the truth) is the established thing that does not change, and *al-ḥaqq* means placing a thing in its proper place. If you displace it from its place, you are the intruder upon it, and the truth must return to its place again. These are only trials and tests, so that the soldiers of the truth may be purified and may have the capacity to carry the call until the Hour is established.

Almighty Allah teaches us: if you see falsehood rise and become high, then take for yourself a lesson from tangible things that fall under your sight, in the origin of life, which is water. Water descends from the sky onto the mountaintops, and it carries with it to the valleys straw, pebbles, and foam. A layer of scum forms atop the water, which is base and of no value. Then, when the winds blow, they push this foam here and there, and the surface of the water remains clean and bright. Thus is the elevation of falsehood: a temporary elevation, and the truth soon returns to its rightful place.

Almighty Allah did not permit falsehood to rise except to show people the distinguishing mark of the truth. When people are afflicted by falsehood, when it hurts them, they cry out against it and long for the truth. Thus falsehood is a soldier among the soldiers of the truth.

As for His words ﴿So whoever is guided, it is for his own self﴾ [al-Zumar: 41], i.e., for its benefit. The Legislator, Almighty Allah, when He legislated for us, sent us messengers and sent down books, gained nothing from that at all. He is not benefited by obedience, nor harmed by disobedience, for by His attributes of absolute perfection He brought you into being, and even prepared for you before He summoned you into existence. By His attribute of perfection He created; He is the Creator before He created anything, just as you say: "So-and-so is a poet," meaning a poet before you have heard any poetry from him, because he would not have composed poetry except that he is a poet.

So: Almighty Allah gains nothing from the worship of people; all the benefit returns to them, because they are His creation, and the craftsman wants his craft to be in good order and in the best state from its beginning to its end, which is toward Him, Almighty.

Since the *sharīʿa* (the divine law) and the method came for the benefit of humanity, whoever is guided, the guidance returns to him, and whoever goes astray, his straying is upon him. ﴿So whoever is guided, it is for his own self, and whoever goes astray, it is only to its detriment﴾ [al-Zumar: 41]. Reflect also here on the meaning of the preposition in *fa-li-nafsihi* ("it is for his own self") and the preposition *ʿalayhā* ("to its detriment"): the benefit of guidance is for you, and the harm of disobedience is upon you.

As for His words ﴿And you are not over them a guardian﴾ [al-Zumar: 41], i.e., you, O Muhammad, are not over them a guardian. The *wakīl* (guardian/agent) is one who has free disposal over those he represents, such that he can compel them and bring them to what he wants.

Almighty Allah did not want this for His Prophet (ﷺ), as He said in another place: ﴿And you are not over them a compeller﴾ [Qaf: 45]. Rather, He wanted him to be a caller with the best of invitations, so that people would come to him willingly, out of love. Had He willed, He would have made them like the angels and created them with an inclination to obedience...

As for His words ﴿And you are not over them a guardian﴾ [al-Zumar: 41], there is in it consolation for our master the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him). It is as if his Lord is saying to him: Do not weary yourself, and do not burden yourself beyond its capacity. Your duty is only to convey. If some harm from them reaches you, know that it does not diminish your standing with them: you are, to them, the truthful and trustworthy one, and they know that you are upon the truth, and your rank with them is great, and their opinion of you is among the best opinions. So do not grieve over their saying about you: "poet," "sorcerer," and "madman." ﴿We know that what they say grieves you; but it is not you they deny, rather it is the signs of Allah that the wrongdoers reject﴾ [al-An'am: 33].

Thus Almighty Allah made the matter His own, and relieved the Messenger of Allah of it. You, O Muhammad, have nothing to blame yourself for; those deniers who wronged you did not deny you except that they rejected My signs.

...Concerning the words of the Exalted: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾. "Al-anfus" is the plural of "nafs" (soul/self), and the nafs is the combined result of the meeting of the material of the body with the spirit (al-ruh), such that the states that exist in the limbs arise from the two of them together. Thus the material alone is not called a nafs, and the spirit alone is not called a nafs.

The meaning of ﴿yatawaffa al-anfus﴾ is: He takes them back to Himself, glory be to Him. The taking of souls by Him has two manifestations: sleep and death. In sleep, a person is deprived of awareness and discernment, while the spirit remains in him to manage the movement of life within him and to sustain it. When he wakes from his sleep, his awareness, his intellect and his discernment return to him. As for death, Allah takes all of it: the awareness, the discernment, and the origin, which is the spirit and the body. The body in sleep does not perform anything, even the brain, which must remain active, does not work in the sleeper except once every seven seconds.

For this reason, when the body's movement stops, its temperature drops and it needs warming. Therefore we advise the sleeper to cover himself, because movement is absent, and the body's heat must be preserved. Some think that the blanket is what warms the sleeper, but the opposite is true: the body's heat is what warms the blanket, and the function of the blanket is to keep the body's heat for you so that it does not dissipate, as evidenced by the fact that you go to your bed and find it cold, and when you wake from your sleep you find it warm.

We have said that a human passes through states: wakefulness, sleep, death, and resurrection. Each stage has its own special law, so beware of mixing one law with another. For example, a person among us, while asleep, loses awareness and discernment, yet he wakes and recounts a dream he saw in which there were shapes, persons and colors that he can distinguish between as if it were wakefulness. By what did he perceive these perceptions and distinguish between the colors while his eye was closed?

They said: because the sleeper has tools and an awareness other than those he has in wakefulness, so he sees, but not with the eye.

So, in the state of death he has another awareness. Some are amazed and perhaps deny that one grave could contain two bodies, one of which is blessed and the other tormented. Why then do you not deny something similar in sleep, for example? You sleep beside someone else in one bed; he sees himself on a pleasant journey full of what is delightful and good, while you see yourself being beaten or going through a painful accident. Neither he knows of you, nor do you know of him.

As for His saying: ﴿So He withholds those on whom He has decreed death﴾ [al-Zumar: 42], meaning: they do not return to the body. ﴿And releases the others...﴾ [al-Zumar: 42], meaning: in the state of sleep, awareness and discernment return to you. ﴿Until an appointed term﴾ [al-Zumar: 42], until the known term which Allah has decreed for you in the Preserved Tablet.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect﴾ [al-Zumar: 42]. Whenever you find one who informs you of something, he alerts in you the faculties of discernment among the concepts, which are the intellect, thought, remembrance and contemplation. So trust that he is sincere toward you, does not deceive you, and does not mislead you, because one who wants to cheat you rushes you along so that you do not know the right course, and does not give you the opportunity to search and to reflect upon the matter...

So whenever the Truthful, glory be to Him, says ("Will you not understand?"), ("Will you not remember?"), ("Will you not reflect?"), know that He is stirring within you the faculties of inquiry, reflection and choosing between alternatives, and He does not do this with you unless He is certain that if you use these faculties you will arrive at nothing but what He wills from you.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (*Tafsir al-Sha'rawi*, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 39, verse 43:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah?﴾ This is a rhetorical question of denial. It means: it was not proper for them to take intercessors besides Allah. The Truth denies this of them after they had heard all these proofs and evidences, and yet they take intercessors besides Allah. Why intercessors besides Allah? They say: because the one who worships other than Allah hopes for himself that he is religious, and religiosity is a disposition in the human soul, from the covenant that Allah took upon it in His words, ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ [al-A'raf: 172].

Therefore the Messengers came as reminders (*muadhdhirin*), that is, to remind us of this first covenant that we had neglected. Recite: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their backs, their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified." [This] lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware." Or [lest] you should say, "Only our fathers associated others with Allah before, and we were descendants after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 172–173].

So the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, denies them that they take intercessors besides Allah, and calls on them to retract this regrettable matter, because taking intercessors besides Allah is a contradiction, since they are intercessors with whom? With Allah. As they said: ﴿We do not worship them except that they bring us nearer to Allah in position﴾ [az-Zumar: 3]. Therefore: they took intercessors so that they would intercede for them with Allah. Then why do they not turn directly to Allah without an intermediary?

Furthermore, intercession is not accepted except with its conditions, and not everyone who wishes to intercede has his intercession accepted. Intercession is not by your own wish. Rather, it is conditional that Allah permit the intercessor to intercede, that He be pleased with the one for whom intercession is made, and that he be among the people of *tawhid* (the affirmation of Allah's oneness). Therefore this intercession they hope for is false and will not be accepted by Allah.

But why do they not turn to Allah in worship without an intermediary? They say: because for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, in His worship there are obligations that may burden the soul, and the path has restrictions: do this and do not do that. They want a religiosity without obligations, and gods without a path and without commands. It is true that they worship idols according to their own desires. But if a matter distresses them and the ways become narrow for them within themselves, they turn to Allah, the true God. Therefore: ﴿Turn back to Allah before there comes a day when there will be no returning...﴾ This verse, ﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah...﴾ [az-Zumar: 43], begins with (*am*), which indicates the coordination (*atf*) of what follows upon what precedes, as if we said: "Was that so, or have they taken [intercessors]?" The preceding speech is His words: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death...﴾ [az-Zumar: 42]. So if you have been entrusted with the strength of your life, your capacity for movement, causes, and transformation, know that Allah gives you a model of death that awaits you through the sleep you undergo.

This death while you are awake is one thing, and when you sleep it is another. He who is able to strip life of discernment, awareness, and movement with the outside (that is, with others) is able to strip it all. For sleep takes from you movement and discernment with others, though movement remains in your being, such as the movement of the heart, the lungs, the intestines, and so on. If Allah has power over this part of you, then He, glorified is He, has power over the other, which is death.

So the meaning is: Have you felt secure about that? And if you do not feel secure, you will die and meet Allah, so why do you take intercessors? And what has reassured you of that? And what is your capital in taking intercessors? That is: Does that happen, or have you taken intercessors?

We have said: the intercessor (*shafi'*) comes from *shaf'*, which is joining one thing to another so that it becomes a pair after having been alone. Allah, glorified is He, wants to end this matter and to show them its falsehood. So He said to them: those you call upon besides Allah do not possess the power to intercede, even if they possessed intercession, as you claim of the angels, and like those who call upon Jesus or Uzayr. They are not pleased with it, and they will not intercede for you.

And if they are from among inanimate things, they are closer to Allah than you are and more knowledgeable than you of the foundations of intercession. It is inevitable that they will reject you and dislike you, even if you possess it and benefit from it. For these inanimate things are in harmony with the cosmos, glorifying their Creator, so they accept only one who glorifies. These inanimate things submitted to you only because Allah subjected them to you and gave you a will by which you control them, by the will and command of Allah, just as you control your limbs. You control the tongue, and you utter with it a word of disbelief; you control the hands, and you strike with them and do wrong, and so on.

All of these do not consent to intercede for you, because you oppose them in the path. Therefore they dislike you, so how would they intercede for you? That is why He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 29].

He attributed weeping to the heaven and the earth. If they do not weep for these opponents, then undoubtedly they weep for those who oppose these who agree with them in creed and path. Therefore the heaven, the earth, and other inanimate things have discernment; otherwise they would not weep for the people of obedience and not weep for the people of disobedience.

Even in literary expression we say: "So-and-so, the earth has rejected him" (*nabat bihi al-ard*), meaning it disliked his residing upon it. Why? Because he is rebellious against Allah and opposed to His path, while the earth is subjected and glorifying. Therefore if he dies, it does not weep for him. Rather, the tongue of its state says to him: "May Allah relieve us of you; may Allah relieve the lands and the servants of you."

Imam Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, explained this matter for us when he said: "When the believer dies, two places weep for him: a place in the heaven and a place in the earth. As for his place in the heaven, it is the ascent of his good deeds," that is, the place where his righteous deed is raised, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿To Him ascends good speech, and righteous deed raises it﴾ [Fatir: 10]. "As for his place in the earth, it is his prayer place."

Therefore, what made them rely on themselves and not fear death is that they took intercessors and thought that these would defend them. But "their tunnel leads to a granary" (*naqbuhum ala shawnah*). For intercession is not by the will of the intercessor, but by the will of the one with whom intercession is made, and He, glorified is He, is the One who permits the intercessor and is pleased with the one for whom intercession is made. But does one with whom Allah is pleased need intercession?

They say: a person may have little good in him, but this little is accompanied by the condition of sincerity (*ikhlas*), so it grows and bears fruit, and Allah compensates for this deficiency by permitting one of His beloved to intercede for him. This intercession was legislated by the Truth, glorified is He, only so that He would accept it and show kindness through it.

Therefore they said: beware of belittling any good deed, however small it may be, for who knows, it may be the cause of your salvation.

As for His words, glorified is He: ﴿Say: "Even though they possess nothing and do not reason?"﴾ That is: these intercessors do not possess anything, and do not understand. The meaning: how do you seek their intercession while they are described in this way?

The verse of God, Exalted be He: ﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah?﴾ [al-Zumar: 43] is a rhetorical interrogative of denunciation (istifham inkari). It means: it was not right for them to take intercessors besides Allah. The Truth denounces them after they have heard all these proofs and evidences, and yet they take intercessors besides Allah. Why intercessors besides Allah? They said: because the one who worships other than Allah hopes for himself that he is religious, and religiosity is a disposition in the human soul, from the covenant that Allah took upon it in ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ [al-A'raf: 172].

Therefore the Messengers came as reminders (muddhakkirin), that is, to remind us of this first covenant that we had neglected. And recite: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify." [This] lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this"* Or lest you say, "Only our fathers associated others with Allah before, and we were [only] descendants after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 172-173].

So the Truth, Exalted be He, denounces them for taking intercessors besides Allah, and calls on them to retract this lamentable matter, because taking intercessors besides Allah is a contradiction. For they are intercessors with whom? With Allah. As they said: ﴿We do not worship them except that they bring us nearer to Allah in position﴾ [al-Zumar: 3]. So they took intercessors in order that they might intercede for them with Allah. Then why do they not turn directly to Allah without an intermediary?

Furthermore, intercession (shafa'ah) is not accepted except under its conditions. Not everyone who wishes to intercede has his intercession accepted. Intercession is not by your own wish; rather, it is conditioned that Allah permit the intercessor to intercede, that He be pleased with the one for whom intercession is made, and that the latter be of the people of tawhid (monotheism). So this intercession that they hope for is false and will not be accepted by Allah.

But why do they not turn to Allah in worship without an intermediary? They said: because Allah, Exalted be He, in His worship has obligations that may burden the soul, and the method has restrictions: do this and do not do that. They want a religiosity without obligations, and gods without a method and without commands. True, they worship idols according to their whims. But if a matter distresses them and the ways become narrow for them within themselves, they turn to Allah, the true God. So: "Return to Allah before the return becomes of no benefit."

The word shafa'ah is derived from ash-shaf' and al-watr (the even and the odd). Ash-shaf' is to join an odd number to an odd number, so that they become a pair (shaf'), that is, a couple.

We have said that the orientalists stopped at two verses of the Book of Allah concerning the matter of intercession, and tried to raise doubt about them, claiming that the Qur'an is not eloquent. They are the verse of God: ﴿And fear a Day when no soul will avail another at all, nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will it be taken from it a ransom, nor will they be helped﴾ [al-Baqarah: 48].

And the other: ﴿And fear a Day when no soul will avail another at all, nor will ransom be accepted from it, nor will intercession benefit it, nor will they be helped﴾ [al-Baqarah: 123].

They said: Which of the two verses is more eloquent than the other? If one of them is eloquent, then the other is not eloquent. Furthermore, what is the wisdom in the advancing and postponing (taqdim and ta'khir) in the two verses, when the meaning is one?

All of this from them is the result of not understanding the language and not having the faculty that tastes and understands from Allah.

We say: You have overlooked the beginning of the verse, ﴿And fear a Day when no soul will avail another at all﴾ [al-Baqarah: 48]. So we have two souls: a soul that recompenses or intercedes, and a soul for which recompense or intercession is made. Which of them is the interceding one and which is the one interceded for? If you mean the soul that is interceded for, then the interceded-for soul first offers ransom, so it is not accepted from it, and so it seeks intercession from one who will intercede for it.

This is the saying of God: ﴿nor will ransom be accepted from it, nor will intercession benefit it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 123]. If you mean the interceding soul, then the intercessor first advances his intercession. If his intercession is not accepted, he offers ransom. He says: "So-and-so, how much do you want from him? I will pay on his behalf." So: the two verses are both eloquent, each according to the meaning intended by it.

This verse ﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah...﴾ [al-Zumar: 43] begins with (am), which conveys the coordination of what follows with what precedes, as if we said: "Was that so, or have they taken?" The preceding discourse is the saying of God: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death...﴾ [al-Zumar: 42]. So if you have been deposited with the strength of your life, your capacity for movement, causes, and transformation, know that Allah gives you a model of death that awaits you through the sleep that you undergo.

This death while you are awake is one thing, and when you sleep it is another. The One who is able to take away life, with its discernment, awareness, and movement toward the outside (that is, toward others), is able to take it all away, because sleep removes from you movement and discernment toward others, though movement remains in your self, such as the movement of the heart, the lungs, the intestines, and so on. If Allah has power over this part of you, then He, Exalted be He, has power over the other, which is death.

So the meaning is: Do you feel secure from that? If you do not feel secure, and you will die and meet Allah, then why do you take intercessors? What reassured you of that? What is your basis for taking intercessors? That is: Will that happen, or have you taken intercessors?

We have said: the intercessor (ash-shafi') is from ash-shaf', which is joining one thing to another, so that it becomes a pair after having been alone. Allah, Exalted be He, wants to put an end to this matter and to show them its falsehood. So He said to them: Those whom you call upon besides Allah do not have the power to intercede, even if they possess intercession, as you call upon the angels, and as those who call upon Isa or Uzayr. They do not consent to it, and they will not intercede for you.

And if they are inanimate objects, they are nearer to Allah than you are and more knowledgeable than you about the fundamentals of intercession. It is inevitable that they will shun you and dislike you, even if you possess it and benefit from it. For these inanimate objects are in harmony with the cosmos, glorifying their Creator, and so they accept only one who glorifies. These inanimate objects submitted to you only because Allah subjected them to you and gave you a will by which you control them, by the will and command of Allah, just as you control your limbs. You control the tongue, so you utter the word of disbelief with it; you control the hands, so you strike with them and do wrong, and so on.

All of them do not consent to intercede for you, because you oppose them in the method. Therefore they dislike you, so how would they intercede for you? That is why He, Exalted be He, said: ﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾ [al-Dukhan: 29].

He affirmed weeping for the heaven and the earth. If they do not weep for these opponents, then undoubtedly they weep for those who are the opposite of these people, who agree with them in belief and method. So the heaven, the earth, and other inanimate things have discernment; otherwise they would not weep for the people of obedience and not weep for the people of disobedience.

Even in our literary expression we say: "So-and-so, the earth has rejected him (nabat bihi al-ard)," meaning it disliked his residing upon it. Why? Because he rebels against Allah and opposes His method, while it is subjected and glorifying. Therefore, if he dies, it does not weep over him. Rather, the state of its condition says to him: "May Allah relieve us of you; may Allah relieve the lands and the servants of you."

Imam Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, has explained this matter for us when he said: "When the believer dies, two places weep for him: a place in the heaven and a place on the earth. As for his place in the heaven, it is the ascending place of his good deed," that is, the place where his righteous deed is raised, as He, Exalted be He, said: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and the righteous deed raises it﴾ [Fatir: 10]. "As for his place on the earth, it is his prayer-place (musallah)."

So: what made them rely on and not fear death is that they took intercessors and thought that they would defend them. But (their tunnel opens onto a granary) (naqbuhum 'ala shawna, an idiom for a hollow, self-defeating scheme), because intercession is not the will of the intercessor; it is the will of the one with whom intercession is made, and He, Exalted be He, is the One who permits the intercessor and is pleased with the one for whom intercession is made. But does one with whom Allah is pleased need intercession?

They said: A person may have few aspects of good, but this little has the condition of sincerity (ikhlas), so He develops it, makes it fruitful, and compensates for this deficiency by permitting one of His beloved to intercede for him. This intercession was legislated by the Truth, Exalted be He, only so that He may accept it and show kindness through it.

Therefore they said: Beware of belittling any good deed, however small it may be, for who knows, it may be the cause of your salvation.

And it has come in a hadith: "Do not belittle any act of obedience," for Allah forgave a man who gave water to a dog panting from intense thirst. He gave it water with effort and resourcefulness, when he found nothing with which to bring water out, so he took off his leather sock and gave the dog water with it. If this man had given water to a human being, we would say he gave it for a reason, or that he had a favor with him. Rather, he gave water to a dog. This indicates that the deed was sincere, because he derived no benefit from the dog; rather, the act of giving water was rooted in his soul. He loves it regardless of the one watered; the man was disposed to good, and he does not care to whom he offers this good.

The second: "A woman entered the Fire because of a cat she confined; she neither fed it nor gave it drink, nor did she let it go to eat from the creatures of the earth." Just as you should not belittle an act of obedience through which your salvation may lie, likewise do not belittle a sin through which your destruction may lie.

The third: "...so do not belittle any creature at all."

And His saying, Exalted be He: ﴿Say: "Even though they had no power over anything and did not understand?"﴾ [al-Zumar: 43]. That is: these intercessors, ﴿who have no power over anything and do not understand﴾ [al-Zumar: 43]. That is: how do you seek their intercession when they are described thus? ﴿Say: "To Allah belongs intercession entirely"﴾ [al-Zumar: 44], because intercession is not except by His permission, He permits the intercessor and is pleased with the one for whom intercession is made. So all intercession belongs to Allah alone, because ﴿to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; then to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-Zumar: 44]. So the arrogant one who rejects my method will return to Me.

Then the Truth, Exalted be He, says:

﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe shrink...﴾ [al-Zumar: 45].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 39, verse 45:

The word (ishmaazzat) means: was repelled (nafarat). When a person hears something he does not like, he shrinks back (yashmaizz), meaning that displeasure appears on his countenance, then a repulsion and a gloomy shudder arise in him, and then he turns away from that thing. Likewise is the state of those people: when they heard the mention of Allah alone, their souls were repelled and they recoiled from the Oneness of Allah. But why?

They said: Because you reminded them of the One in whom they fully trust to possess their harm and their benefit. Otherwise, if they did not have this trust, the mention of Allah would have had no effect on their souls. So their hearts shrank because they feared something; and when they heard the mention of Allah, they remembered His majesty, His power and His greatness, and they remembered that they were coming toward Him, standing before Him, and had not prepared for that standing.

The word alone (wahdahu) indicates their inclination toward the partners. The meaning is: if the partners were mentioned, their hearts would not have shrunk. The shrinking of the hearts is an unseen matter that shows on the face through emotion, so it appears on the face that it is contracted with a painful contraction. The verse did not mention why their hearts shrank, which indicates that the heart is the mover that gives the limbs their emotion according to what happens to things. For example, you meet a person and find yourself delighted, and another you meet and find yourself concerned or withdrawn from him. From where do these emotions come? From the heart.

As for His saying: ﴿And when those besides Him are mentioned﴾, i.e., the partners, ﴿behold, they rejoice﴾, i.e., they are glad. Why? Because they think that they will intercede for them. But they are disappointed in this, and disappointed in that.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 39, verse 46:

This is a command from God Most High to His Messenger ﷺ, after He had mentioned the promise for the people of good and the warning for the people of evil, and had fulfilled both matters with both groups. He said to His Messenger, after you have conveyed the promise and the warning: you have no part in this except to take refuge in God. He alone, glory be to Him, is the One who judges between you and these people, because you have exhausted with them every aspect of good call and beautiful conveyance. As long as they remain obstinate, leave them until God judges between you and them on the Day of Resurrection.

And do not grieve, O Muhammad, for God only judges with truth. Be certain that it is He who chose you for the message, that He is your helper and the one who makes your religion prevail, and you will see this victory in this world before the Hereafter. Indeed, the Messenger saw it before his death...

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, teaches His Messenger ﷺ, and teaches us, how to call upon Him. He said: (Say) i.e., O Muhammad (Allahumma). Our master Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib says: I do not find in the Qur'an a verse more hopeful for the one who calls upon God than His saying, glory be to Him: "Say: O God (Allahumma), Originator of the heavens and the earth..." And God only taught him to call upon Him because He had preceded in decree that He would answer. Therefore, the Truth, glory be to Him, did not leave His Messenger to call upon Him with a wording of his own; rather He taught him what to call upon Him with, so acceptance is bound to be written for him, just as if a person gave you the key; this means he accepts you entering the place.

Here we must pause at the eloquence of the expression and the greatness of the supplication and the call in (Allahumma). It is the Divine Name (Allah) to which a doubled (shadda) mim has been attached for supplication and calling. We know that the vocative (nida') is a request for the addressee to turn toward the speaker, and the vocative has known particles according to the nearness or distance of the one called. We say for a nearby one: "Amuhammad" (a-Muhammad). For a distant one: "Ya Muhammad," and for the farthest: "Aya Muhammad," etc.

Therefore, the vocative particle itself determines the location of the one called. Is it permissible to use these particles in calling upon the Truth, glory be to Him, so that we say, for example: "Ya Allah"? It is from the etiquette in calling upon God, glory be to Him, that we do not call Him as we call others, because He, glory be to Him, is nearer to us than the jugular vein. Thus it is not correct to say "Ya Allah" or "Aya Allah," for these are degrees of distance, and God is near.

For this reason you will not find the Qur'an using these particles at all in calling upon Him, glory be to Him; rather it used "Allahumma" for supplication and taught us to call upon Him with it. It attached the doubled mim instead of the vocative particles before the called name. The mim is a substitute for the omitted vocative particle, so the doubled mim indicates the call and the humility of the request from you.

When we survey the Noble Qur'an, we find that the word Allah occurs in the nominative case 985 times, and there is no supplication in it except with "Allahumma," in five places: this verse before us; then His saying, exalted be He: "Say: O God (Allahumma), Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty from whom You will, You honour whom You will and You abase whom You will..." [Al 'Imran: 26].

And His saying: "Isa son of Maryam said: O God (Allahumma), our Lord, send down to us a table from the heaven to be for us a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You; and provide for us, and You are the best of providers" [al-Ma'idah: 114].

And His saying: "And when they said: O God (Allahumma), if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment" [al-Anfal: 32].

And His saying: "Their call therein is: Glory be to You, O God (Allahumma), and their greeting therein is peace, and the last of their call is: Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds" [Yunus: 10].

As for calling upon the Lordship, we say: "Ya Rabb" (O Lord). There is a difference between calling the Name of Majesty (Allah) and calling the Name of Lordship (Rabb). Divinity (uluhiyyah) is an obligation, whereas Lordship (rububiyyah) is bestowal and giving. Since the Lord is the giver of blessing, we say in calling Him: "Ya Rabb," because Lordship is bringing into existence from non-existence, supplying from nothingness, and nurturing. Thus you are the beneficiary of the gift of Lordship, whereas divinity is an obligation: do this and do not do that.

As for the word Fatir, it means: the creator, originator, and bringer into existence of being from nothing, without a prior pattern. That is, an innovative new matter. If the bringing into existence follows a prior pattern, meaning imitation, it is not called Fatir.

As for His saying "the heavens and the earth," He chose the heavens and the earth because they are the existence that never leaves a person: the earth carries him and the sky shades him, so he is never separated from them for a moment of his life. There are other blessings that may be absent from a person at times, such as water, for example.

"Knower of the unseen and the seen": God Most High mentions His knowledge of the unseen. How then does He mention His knowledge of the seen, which is known to people and witnessed?

They said: because God is unseen. We may understand that this unseen is like the unseen relative to you: you see who is with you in the house, but you do not see who is outside the house, so he is unseen to you. But the Truth, glory be to Him, knows the unseen and knows the witnessed, what is absent from you and what is witnessed by you and by others.

His saying: "You will judge between Your servants concerning that in which they have been differing" [al-Zumar: 46 continued in the next part]. This is the final reference in the dispute between truth and falsehood, on the day of victory that these people awaited and hastened, and even mocked it, as He, glory be to Him, said recounting them: "Then bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the truthful" [al-A'raf: 70].

And they say: "When will this victory be, if you should be truthful?" [al-Sajdah: 28]. The Truth, glory be to Him, replies to them: "Say: On the day of victory, the disbelievers' faith will not benefit them, nor will they be reprieved" [al-Sajdah: 29], meaning: if this day comes to you, you will not return afterward to find faith or repentance.

We note here that the Qur'an used the word "servants" (ibad) to denote both groups: the believers and the disbelievers. Generally the word "servants" is used for the obedient who adhere to the method, as in His saying, glory be to Him: "And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, 'Peace'" [al-Furqan: 63].

Is the term "servants" also said of disbelievers and sinners?

They said: yes, because a person has two states in relation to his Lord, exalted be He. One state in which he has choice, which is the power of choice God created in man, by which he does what he wills, even doing what his Lord does not want from him. And there is another state in which he has no choice, which are the compelled matters in which the servant has no option.

So a person, for example, may rebel against the method of his Lord, oppose it and deviate from it, and we say to him: since you have become accustomed to rebellion, then rebel against everything: rebel against sickness, rebel against death... He cannot, because these are compelled matters in which he has no choice. Thus in this state he is subjected to servitude by compulsion; he does not leave his servitude to God even if he is a disbeliever. And when we say "servants" to the disbelievers, it is because in the side of their conduct where they do not rebel against God, they are compelled.

Therefore God said of them in the Hereafter: "Did you lead these My servants astray, or did they themselves stray from the way?" [al-Furqan: 17].

This is an address to those who led others astray, yet He called the misguided "servants." Why? Because the discourse here concerns the Hereafter, where all are equal: there everyone is obedient, righteous, and faithful; all are servants and slaves there. But in this world, all are slaves, and some of them are servants.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 39, verse 47:

You remember that we said, in discussing intercession (*shafa'ah*), that the sinner is presented before his Lord, may He be exalted, to offer a ransom so that he may be forgiven, but no ransom is accepted from him. He then brings someone to intercede for him, but his intercession is rejected. Let us suppose that he has the whole world in its entirety, owns it, and offers it as a ransom for his sins, and even more than that: he has everything that is on earth, all of it, ﴿and the like of it along with it﴾ [al-Zumar 39:47]. Yet this situation has never happened to anyone. But suppose it had happened, and the disobedient person offered all of that to ransom himself from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. It would not be accepted from him.

His, may He be glorified, saying ﴿they would ransom themselves with it from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Zumar 39:47] shows that a person, before he secures bliss for himself, wants to be saved from punishment, and this is the more important matter. This is why the arrogant man, the owner of the two gardens in Surah al-Kahf, when he was deceived by his deeds and thought them righteous, said: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a destination﴾ [al-Kahf 18:36]. That is, he meant: He will give me better than what I had. This is delusion, and we seek refuge in Allah.

Likewise, you find that a rich man, when a severe illness strikes him, we seek refuge in Allah, says: "Take everything I own and restore my health to me." He wants first to be freed from the illness he is in. Such is the condition of the people of disobedience in the Hereafter.

The meaning of ﴿the evil of the punishment﴾ [al-Zumar 39:47] is: the punishment that is evil, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Zumar 39:47]. Then there will confront them what they did not reckon: ﴿and there will appear to them from Allah that which they had not been counting on﴾ [al-Zumar 39:47]. "Badā" means: it became apparent to them, because however much a person imagines in this world, his imagination will never be broad enough to encompass what Allah brings about in the Hereafter.

This is why our master Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir said: "This verse has frightened me, for I fear that when I die there will appear to me what I had not reckoned. A person often commits evil deeds without feeling them, or without knowing that they are evil deeds, or he may commit them and forget them. This is what Allah referred to in His saying: ﴿Allah has enumerated it, while they have forgotten it﴾ [al-Mujadilah 58:6]."

Satan may also make evil seem attractive to you, so you see it as good when it is not good. All of this you will be confronted with in the Hereafter.

The first thing that will confront the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection is that they will not find the deities they worshipped besides Allah, and they will not intercede for them. Even their leaders and chiefs who misled them will disown them: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed, and they see the punishment, and their bonds are cut off﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:166].

Indeed, the misleading leaders will enter the Fire before their followers, as the Qur'an recounts: ﴿This is a troop rushing in with you; no welcome for them. They will surely burn in the Fire. They will say, "Rather, it is you; no welcome for you. You brought this upon us, so what an evil residence!" They will say, "Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, increase him in punishment double in the Fire"﴾ [Sad 38:59–61].

Had the follower entered before his leader, his thoughts would have been attached to him, and he would have thought that the leader would come to him and deliver him. But he will enter and find that the leader has preceded him, and then their hopes will be cut off, and regret and remorse will be complete.

Then the Truth, may He be glorified, says:

﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they earned…﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 39, verse 48:

His saying "and there will appear to them" (wa-badā lahum): i.e., there will become manifest to them and clear to them. "The evil deeds" (sayyi'āt): is what appears to them in the Hereafter the evil deeds, or the punishment for the evil deeds? The scholars said: what they see in the Hereafter is the punishment for the evil deeds, but He said "there will appear to them the evil deeds of what they earned" (wa-badā lahum sayyi'ātu mā kasabū), because the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. So the punishment is also "evil deeds," as He, glorified is He, said: "and the recompense for an evil deed is an evil deed like it" [al-Shura: 40], because the meaning of sayyi'ah (evil deed) is the thing that causes distress; just as he did evil in action in this world, We cause him evil in the Hereafter.

As for the word "what they earned" (mā kasabū) [al-Zumar: 48], we have already clarified this matter earlier and said: the Qur'an uses kasaba (to earn) for good and iktasaba (to acquire) for evil, because good comes from a person naturally, without effort or stratagem, so it comes in the pattern (fa'ala). Evil, however, requires from its doer effort, concealment and stratagem, so it is expressed by what indicates artifice, which is (iftaʿala) or iktasaba.

We gave an example of this: a person looks at the members of his household or his close relatives, among whom there may be beautiful women, for instance. He looks with a natural look that he does not conceal, and he fears nothing in it. But if he wishes to look at a woman who is not lawful to him, he hides this look and resorts to every means for it.

So: why did the Qur'an here use the word kasaba in the domain of evil deeds, when, as we have explained, it is iktisāb? Similar to it is His saying, exalted is He: "Nay, whoever earns an evil deed, and his sin has encompassed him" [al-Baqarah: 81].

The scholars said: the Qur'an used kasaba for evil deeds because the doer of an evil deed may become accustomed to it until it becomes a nature in him, a habit and a practised skill; indeed, it may become for him a skill to the point of boasting of it, God forbid. These people do evil without effort and without concealment, so for them it is kasb, not iktisāb. An example of this is criminals who have become accustomed to crime and trained in it; for them it is a natural process, and when they do an evil deed they count it a gain for themselves.

As for His saying, "and there will surround them what they used to mock at" (wa-ḥāqa bihim mā kānū bihi yastahzi'ūn) [al-Zumar: 48], i.e., there will descend upon them what they used to mock at. This meaning was made clear by the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He: "Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they winked at one another. And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting. And when they saw them, they said, 'Indeed, these are the astray.' But they had not been sent as guardians over them. So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, upon couches, looking on. Have the disbelievers been recompensed for what they used to do?" [al-Mutaffifin: 29–36].

Yes... we often see and hear the mockery of the people of falsehood against the people of truth, their ridicule of them and their derision of them, and the matter reaches the point that they accuse them of being in error. Glory be to God! But the consolation of the people of truth is that this mockery is in the transient world, and if they are patient with it, they have a reward; and this mockery and derision will be returned in the enduring Hereafter, where the people of truth will mock the people of falsehood and laugh at them. Indeed the Truthful, glorified is He, addresses them to comfort their hearts: "Have the disbelievers been recompensed for what they used to do?" [al-Mutaffifin: 36], meaning: have We determined to repay them with what they deserve?

The scholars said: the mockery of the wicked against the good, and his derision of him, is a revenge for the goodness of the other upon his wickedness, because he cannot and is not able to be like him, so he mocks him and ridicules him, perhaps so that he turns away from the good he is in and goes to evil. But the intelligent person understands this matter and knows that this mockery is rage, hatred and envy, so he bears it patiently, knowing that for every mockery and every derision he has a station with God, and for that he has a recompense.

We have seen the polytheists who took other gods besides God and said: "We only worship them so that they may bring us near to God in closeness" (﴿ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى﴾). When some calamity befalls them, or something beyond the capacity of their means occurs in their lives, they do not turn to the idols, nor to the gods they worshipped besides God. Rather, they turn to God and entreat Him, exalted is He, that He may remove from them what they are in and lift the affliction from them. Why?

Because this is the sound nature (fitrah) upon which God created people, and the covenant that God took from all of us while we were in the world of atoms (ʿalam al-dharr), when He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: ﴿Yes, we testify.﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 172]. A person does not deceive himself or surrender himself to others. So when evil surrounds him and the means cannot rise to repel it, he says: "O Lord!" At that moment he forgets his arrogance, forgets his obstinacy, forgets his denial of the messengers, and finds none but his Lord, his Creator, and his true God.

God has spoken the truth: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish except Him. But when He brings you safely to the land, you turn away. And man has always been ungrateful.﴾ [al-Isra: 67]...

As for His saying: ﴿Then when We bestow upon him a favor from Us,﴾ i.e., when We give him a blessing, ﴿he says: "I was only given it because of knowledge."﴾ [al-Zumar: 49], meaning: if We give him a blessing after this harm that touched him, he soon forgets and returns to his arrogance and worldly conceit, because he fears that the removal of harm from him will bring him closer to the Lord who answered his call, and that this favor which his Lord granted him will return him to the right path and to uprightness.

Uprightness (istiqamah) entails obligations and responsibility, which he dislikes; he does not want to bind himself to them, because obligation (taklif) means restraining the self from its desires and compelling it to obedience. So he fears that this matter will confine him or restrict his freedom in desires. Therefore the Truth, exalted is He, said about prayer: ﴿And indeed it is burdensome, except upon the humble﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45].

As for His saying: ﴿I was only given it because of knowledge,﴾ it has two possible meanings: either it is knowledge from God that I deserve this good, for otherwise He would not have given it to me (this if he believes that God is the Giver), or it is knowledge from me, because I have precision in dealing and alertness, I have experience and understanding of affairs, and I study outcomes.

Here his Lord corrects him: ﴿Nay, it is a trial﴾ (bal hiya fitnah). That is: this blessing is a trial from God. It is neither because God knew you deserved it, nor is it the result of your knowledge and skill. ﴿Nay, it is a trial﴾ means a test and an examination. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial﴾ [al-Anbiya: 35]: We test with evil to see who is patient, and we test with good to see who is thankful and who transgresses.

And in another place He, exalted, said: ﴿And We have made some of you a trial for others: will you be patient?  And your Lord is ever Seeing﴾ [al-Furqan: 20].

That is: each of us is a trial for the other. The rich is a trial for the poor, and the strong is a trial for the weak, and the reverse is also true, so that the Truth, exalted is He, may test His creation: who is patient and who is impatient, who is thankful and who is ungrateful, who is content and who is resentful.

Therefore, a person should, in the movement of his life, establish what God has established. Everything that God makes to pass over him is good. If you see a blessing with someone else that you do not have, know that God has not favored him over you, and by your patience with what has been decreed for you and by not harboring envy toward your brother, you can become better than him.

The verse concludes with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ (wa lakinna aktharahum la yaʿlamun). That is: these truths that have been mentioned are not known to most people, which means that only a few know.

Then Almighty God makes clear that this matter is not merely a theoretical statement; it is a reality with precedent in the history of those before us. He says: ﴿Those before them had already said it, but what they used to earn did not avail them﴾ [az-Zumar: 50]. Indeed, Qarun said it: ﴿I was only given it on knowledge I possess﴾ [al-Qasas: 78].

We say: since you were given it on knowledge, whether knowledge from God that you are worthy of this good, or knowledge in yourself and skill in work and handling, here is the blessing before you, and there is nothing for you but to preserve it. Preserving a thing that is already in your hands is easier than bringing it into existence from nothing. So can you do it?

The meaning is that I am not speaking to you in theory; it is a reality attested by history. Qarun said it and was deceived by it, and then We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. Here a question arises: if you were given it on knowledge, then preserve it too with knowledge. But since the matter has already abandoned you in preservation, which is easy, then you are even more remote from being able to create it.

Indeed, ﴿Those before them had already said it, but what they used to earn did not avail them﴾ [az-Zumar: 50], because God caused the earth to swallow Qarun and his home as well. So the blessing and the wealth were not lost alone; the retribution reached even the land and the place where he lived, slept, and rested.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 39, verse 51:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So the evil of what they earned befell them﴾ [Az-Zumar: 51], meaning: those before them who said this word, the evil of what they earned befell them and descended upon them. That is, they did it to themselves, ﴿and We did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾. ﴿And those who wronged among these [people]﴾ [Az-Zumar: 51], meaning: the contemporaries [of the Prophet], ﴿the evil of what they earned will strike them, and they will not escape [it]﴾ [Az-Zumar: 51].

The mu'jiz (one who causes incapacity, i.e., the miracle-working agent) is one who performs a deed by which he challenges you, and you are unable to produce its like. Therefore we call the sign of the truthfulness of the messengers in conveying from God a mu'jiza (miracle), because it renders the obstinate denier incapable, whereas one who believes merely upon the conveying and affirms it has no need of a miracle. The miracle is required to be accompanied by a challenge. Why?

They said: because when you challenge him and inform him that you will perform a deed he cannot match, you thereby stir up his faculties so that he prepares for the confrontation, and then you can establish the proof against him. But if you surprise him with the challenge, he may say to you: "By God, if I had considered the matter, or if it had been in my mind, I would have done it." Thus: mu'jiz means that it strikes the other with incapacity to match it.

We have said regarding the miracle that it should be of the kind in which the people excelled, and suited to the age in which the challenge is made, because if you challenged a people with something of which they had no knowledge or practice, they would have the right to say: "If we had known this, we would have done it," and otherwise there would be no place for the challenge.

The noble Qur'an has given us a model of challenge when it challenged the Arabs, who were the people of language and the masters of eloquence and expression. It challenged them to produce the like of this Qur'an. When we reflect on this challenge, we find it proceeds in descending stages, and the lower it descends in its challenge, the higher it rises in its inimitability. For at first it challenged them to produce the like of this Qur'an, then to ten surahs, then to a single surah like it.

Not only this, but it extended the challenge from mankind to the jinn, because although the Arabs were a people of speech and eloquence, they attributed to the jinn a higher capacity for eloquence and rhetoric, as evidenced by the fact that when a poet among them excelled, they said: "The jinn reveal these meanings to him," and they believed that these jinn dwell in the Valley of 'Abqar, as they say.

Therefore the Qur'an moved the challenge from the realm of mankind to the realm of the jinn, and He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to one another assistants﴾ [Al-Isra: 88], meaning: supporters and helpers.

Therefore the miracle of Prophet Musa, peace be upon him, was a kind of magic, because his people excelled in it, and the miracle of Prophet 'Isa, peace be upon him, was that he healed the blind and the leper by God's permission, because his people excelled in medicine.

As for the phrase ﴿and they will not escape [it]﴾ [Az-Zumar: 51], meaning: in fleeing and escaping punishment, because they did things deserving of punishment; so when We seize them for punishment, they will not render Us incapable. That is: they will not slip away from Us. For with regard to us, your debtor may be in your hand and in the same place as you, or he may flee from you to another place; but with regard to the Truth, glorified is He, He is in every place. Otherwise, show me a place in which Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is not. Then how is flight, and where to? If you are with Him, He will not be unable to reach you, and if you flee, He will not be unable to bring you back.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 39, verse 52:

Because Qarun was deceived by his wealth and his standing, and by the riches and pride he had among his people, he said: ﴿He said, "I was only given it on account of knowledge I possess."﴾ [al-Qasas: 78]. So the Truth, glorified is He, wanted to correct this notion for him and for those who were of his kind, and He said: ﴿Do they not know that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it?﴾ [al-Zumar: 52]. "Yabsut" (extends) means He widens it for whom He wills, and "yaqdir" means He constricts it for whom He wills and withholds it. As we say: He gives to one who has no resourcefulness, so that the one who has resourcefulness may marvel.

So then: the matter of provision and giving is not a matter of cleverness and skill in handling things; rather, it is a measure decreed by the Provider, glorified is He.

It has come in the hadith qudsi, the saying of the Exalted: [text not given in the passage]. Provision is apportioned by the Provider, glorified is He; it does not depend on skill, sound judgment, or good thinking. Therefore Abu al-'Atahiyya said:

"The fool is given abundant provision,
while the man of intellect is deprived and distressed."

And Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, provides for a person from where he does not expect. It is related that a shepherd, as he was walking along the road, stumbled over a stone with his foot, and he found beside it a well. He began to feel about in the well, and he found something that made a sound (shakhshakha) like the sound of gold and silver. He searched for it and found it was a sack full of gold and silver. He took from it what would fill his pockets and what he could carry, and he left the rest in a place he knew, so that he could return to it when he needed it.

After some time the money he had ran out, so he came to the same place to take from this wealth, and he found another person had got there before him and had taken what remained of it. When he saw him carrying it on his back, he looked at him. The man said: "Allah has provided me with what I had thought was yours, but it is mine."

Yet we notice, regarding provision, that people err when they think of provision as limited to wealth alone. For them, provision is riches and abundance of money, but the correct view is that provision is everything from which one benefits and profits. Accordingly, knowledge is provision, forbearance is provision, trustworthiness is provision, health is provision, and so on.

Therefore the wealthy man who has been given abundant wealth ought to ask himself when he sees a poor man: what is this poor man's provision, and in what does he differ from me? Perhaps his provision lies in his intellect, or his manners, or his forbearance, or his good reputation among people, or his well-being.

We have said before that the total of gifts in any person equals the total of gifts in another. This one has wealth at a rate of ten out of ten, but he is deprived of the blessing of children at a rate of zero out of ten, and so on; for all creation are the dependents of Allah, and none of them is the son of Allah or has a kinship with Allah.

So then: on what does distinction between one person and another rest? We say: provision requires multiple sources; therefore the Provider, glorified is He, distributes the means, so life would not be sound if people were all rich, or all intelligent or all scholars. For a single mind, for example, needs more than one limb to serve its thinking. The engineer, when he draws the design of a residential building, is a single engineer, but he needs a number of workers to carry out this work and to serve this engineering idea. The simple labourer who digs the earth to lay the foundations has gifts that the engineer does not have. Thus gifts are distributed and provisions are distributed.

Provision may come by an increase in income, or it may come negatively, by a decrease in expenditure. We find, for example, a man whose monthly salary is a hundred pounds, and people wonder how he lives on this sum, forgetting that what matters in provision is that it be lawful; Allah blesses the little of it so that it takes the place of much. So you find this man, for example, when his child is ill, is sufficed by a tablet of aspirin, and the mother prepares him a cup of tea, and the child recovers by Allah's permission.

Whereas another obtains many times this sum, but does not seek what is lawful in his earning. When his child falls ill, he takes him to the doctor, orders tests, and convinces himself that the illness is grave, so that he spends large sums on the child.

Therefore the noble hadith says: "Whoever acquires wealth from dubious sources, Allah will cause it to vanish in ruinous ways."

So then: the provision of increase is that the income grows, and the provision of reduction is that the expenditure decreases. Thus we notice, for example, an official with a high salary and a colleague with a modest salary who go to the market. The first buys Roman fish or sea bream at ten pounds a kilo, while the other buys ordinary fish at, say, four pounds a kilo. Each goes home and each eats fish, but the first has spent many times what the other has, and perhaps the result is the same, and each is content with what he took and what he ate. We call this the provision of reduction.

The believer should always keep economy in his expenditure in mind, and know that the provision of reduction is broader than the provision of increase, because the provision of reduction prevents pain, whereas the provision of increase may bring pain.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ [al-Zumar: 52], that is: who believe in the Provider who named Himself the Extender and named Himself the Restrainer. Since the Truth, glorified is He, named Himself the Extender and named Himself the Restrainer, each attribute must have an object of its action, and there must exist among creation one to whom Allah extends provision and one upon whom He restricts and constricts it, and both this and that are by His wisdom and His decree, glorified is He.

So whoever has his provision widened by Allah and extended to him should give thanks; and whoever has his provision measured out and constricted for him must be patient and content, and must go about the course of his life according to his provision, and not open for himself the doors of begging. Whoever is content with his lot, Allah gives him according to his measure, glorified is He. Therefore you will find that the great men of the world, and those of renown and reputation, if you look at them in the beginnings of their lives, you will find they were content with Allah's decree concerning them and lived within the level of their income, so that there was fulfilled in them His saying: "Whoever is content with My decree, I shall give him according to his measure."

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves...﴾.

The commentary of al-Sha'rawi on surah 39, verse 53:

Al-israf (excess, extravagance) is going beyond the limit. We say: "So-and-so is musrif (extravagant)," meaning he exceeds the limit in spending in a way that does not match his income. These people were musrifun against themselves ("ʿala anfusihim") and it was not said "li-anfusihim" (for their own benefit). Rather, they were extravagant against them (ʿalayha), which indicates that this excess draws ruin upon them. It is excess in sins and wrongdoings, God forbid.

We have said that al-israf is going beyond the limit. If the limit follows a command, then do not transgress it. If it follows a prohibition, He says "do not approach it," meaning merely do not come near it, because God says regarding commands: ﴿These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:229], meaning stop at them. As for prohibitions, He says: ﴿These are the limits of God, so do not approach them﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:187], because your approaching a thing tempts you toward it. And as is mentioned in the noble hadith: therefore, when God (exalted is He) forbade our master Adam from eating from the tree, He did not say to him "do not eat from it," but said: ﴿And do not approach this tree﴾ [al-Aʿraf 7:19].

Therefore you find that the word ijtinab (avoidance, keeping away) is stronger and more intense than the word tahrim (prohibition). It is strange that we hear from those who are extravagant against themselves that they say: "No word prohibiting wine has come in the Book of God." We reply: How, when there has come something stronger than prohibition, which is ijtinab, in His words: ﴿Indeed, wine, gambling, stone idols, and divining arrows are only defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may succeed. Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred to occur among you through wine and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of God and from prayer. So will you not desist?﴾ [al-Maʾidah 5:90-91].

Because the meaning of ﴿fa-ijtanibuhu﴾ (so avoid it) is: keep away from it completely. Avoid its gathering, avoid its drinker, avoid its seller, avoid its carrier, and so on. This is more emphatic in prohibition than our saying "do not drink wine." The proof is that the Qur'an used the word ijtinab at the summit of creedal faith, when He said: ﴿So avoid the defilement of idols and avoid the saying of falsehood﴾ [al-Hajj 22:30].

When we take up extravagance in spending, we find that God the Glorified desires that the movement of life in the believing society be a balanced, equitable movement that moderates matters. This means that you know your income and your provision which God drives to you. God does not want you to hold this provision tightly and not spend from it, nor does He want you to spend all of it or be extravagant with it, but He desires moderation, as He explained: ﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but are ever, between that, justly moderate﴾ [al-Furqan 25:67]. So both extravagance and stinginess are blameworthy and forbidden. Whoever takes a path other than the middle path harms himself and society, because if he withholds money, the power to buy and sell in the markets decreases, and this results in stagnation in commercial and industrial movement, goods going to waste, and slump in the market.

And if he is extravagant and squanders, spending all his income, he finds nothing to save with which to grow his life, improve his standard, and advance his living. At that point he blames himself, because he sees others advancing and enjoying their lives while he cannot.

God the Glorified clarified this meaning in His saying: ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck, nor extend it fully outstretched, lest you sit blamed and destitute﴾ [al-Isra' 17:29].

The meaning: "blamed" when you withhold and are miserly, "destitute" when you are extravagant and squander, because he will find that the people of moderation live the life of the happy, with no blame and no regret. The intelligent person is one who makes his expenditure subject to his income, not one who makes his income subject to his expenditure. Because when you make your income subject to your expenditure, your hand will inevitably extend to borrow from people, and this will exhaust and burden you. Your means will run out, people will withdraw their hearts from you, you will become insignificant in their eyes, and as a result you will live in distress.

So we say: al-israf is going beyond the limit in what returns to you with evil and harm. Therefore He (exalted is He) said: ﴿They who have been extravagant against themselves﴾ [al-Zumar 39:53]. As for the extravagance that returns to you with good, it is extravagance for you, not against you, like the one who pays the zakat on his wealth at ten percent instead of 2.5 percent, because he is certain that this is what remains for him, and what is saved with God. One person works only for the affairs of his worldly life, and another works for both this world and the Hereafter.

Therefore, when Imam ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) was asked: "O Imam, I want to know, am I from the people of this world or from the people of the Hereafter?" He said: "I do not have an answer to this question; its answer is with you." He said: "How?" He said: "If two people enter upon you: one with a gift, and the other wanting charity or assistance, look at which of them you greet with cheer and welcome. If you welcome the one with the gift, you are from the people of this world, because you love the one who builds your worldly life. If it is the other, you are from the people of the Hereafter, because you love the one who builds your Hereafter."

And you know the story of the sheep which— So: what remains is what we have given in charity, and what goes is what we have eaten. This hadith is supported by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the hadith: Then God the Glorified opens a window of hope for those who have been extravagant against themselves, and says to them: ﴿Do not despair of the mercy of God﴾ [al-Zumar 39:53]. Despair (qunut) is hopelessness regarding God's mercy. But why would we despair of God's mercy? They said: because they were extravagant against themselves, exceeded in disobedience, and persisted in it. When the one who was extravagant returns and repents, he blames himself and reproaches himself, and his sins become great in his eyes. He does not see himself as deserving forgiveness or mercy, so despair enters him, God forbid.

Whoever reflects finds that this self-blame and this despair of mercy is, from another angle, a healthy sign in faith, because magnifying sins and the extravagant person not seeing himself as deserving of mercy indicates the soundness of his faith and his fear of his Lord.

His saying (exalted is He): ﴿Indeed, God forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [al-Zumar 39:53].

Ibn ʿAbbas said of this verse that it is the most hopeful verse in the Book of God, because it gives hope to every sinner, however great his sins. And had God not followed it with His saying: ﴿And turn in repentance to your Lord and submit to Him﴾ [al-Zumar 39:54], it would have bred complacency among people and given them such an appetite for God's mercy that it would make them forget His punishment and vengeance. The believer moves in the movement of his life between fear and hope, and he needs both together.

Yes, your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful, but in order for you to be a place for this mercy and attached to this forgiveness, you must turn back to God and return to Him with sincere, devoted return, because the one who sins and repents, then sins and repents again, is like one who mocks his Lord, and we seek refuge in God from this.

When Ibn ʿAbbas said about this verse that it is the most hopeful verse in the Book of God, one of his companions said: "I see that the most hopeful verse in the Book of God is His saying: ﴿And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for people despite their wrongdoing﴾ [al-Raʿd 13:6]. And I criticize the scholars who explain ʿala zulmihim (despite their wrongdoing) as meaning maʿa zulmihim (along with their wrongdoing), and this does not stand. The meaning of the verse, such that we say it is the most hopeful verse in the Book of God, and we note here that maʿa has two letters while ʿala has three letters. So the meaning that ʿala conveys is necessarily not conveyed by maʿa, because since there is forgiveness of sin here, and sin requires the attributes of the Subduer, the Compeller, and the Avenger, yet God's forgiveness rises above sin and erases it, and this meaning is not conveyed by maʿa."

Here is a pause for the Orientalists who try to disparage the style of the Qur'an, who saw a contradiction between His saying here: ﴿Indeed, God forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [al-Zumar 39:53], and His saying (exalted is He): ﴿Indeed, God does not forgive that partners should be associated with Him﴾ [al-Nisaʾ 4:48].

We say to them: your ignorance of the language of the Qur'an and the features of its style led you into this error, because sin means committing a crime that God has forbidden and assigned a punishment for, and associating partners with God is not a sin in this sense, because shirk removes its practitioner from the religious community (millah) altogether. Accordingly, there is no contradiction between the two verses as you suppose.

They said: this verse was revealed: ﴿Say: O My servants who have been extravagant against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God…﴾ [al-Zumar 39:53]. It was revealed concerning Wahshi, who killed our master Hamzah at Uhud, when Hind took the liver of our master Hamzah and chewed it. We say: Hamzah was killed at Uhud, and Wahshi did not embrace Islam after that; rather, he embraced it after a long period.
