As He, glorified is He, said in another place: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَآءَ أَحَدَهُمُ ٱلْمَوْتُ قَالَ رَبِّ ٱرْجِعُونِ﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 99] ("until, when death comes to one of them, he says: My Lord, send me back"). All these are false wishes, so do not believe them; were they returned, they would revert to what they were, and just as they lied in the first [statement], ﴿لَوْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هَدَانِي﴾ [Az-Zumar: 57], they lied in ﴿فَأَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ [Az-Zumar: 58].

Lying may be conceived of in a person in the world, but it is strange that he should lie in the Hereafter, while standing before his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. Therefore the Truth will say after it: ﴿وَيَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ تَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَبُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ وُجُوهُهُم مُّسْوَدَّةٌ﴾ [Az-Zumar: 60] ("And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied against God, their faces blackened").

It appears that lying (clung) to them, and they became accustomed to it, to the point that they carried it with them into the Hereafter.

Then the Truth responds to this lie, saying, Exalted is He:

﴿بَلَىٰ قَدْ جَآءَتْكَ آيَاتِي فَكَذَّبْتَ بِهَا وَٱسْتَكْبَرْتَ...﴾ ("Yes! My signs did come to you, but you denied them and were arrogant...").

The word (بَلَى) is a particle of response that comes only after a negation, and it affirms the meaning that was negated before it. As in His saying, ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ [al-A'raf: 172], the answer is ﴿They said: Yes, indeed!﴾ [al-A'raf: 172], meaning: "No, You are our Lord." The rule is that the negation of a negation is an affirmation. Similarly, ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾ [al-Tin: 8]. Whoever hears it should say: "Yes, O Lord," meaning: "No, You are the most just of judges."

So where is the negation that precedes His saying here, ﴿Yes, indeed! My revelations did come to you﴾ [al-Zumar: 59]? Some have said that it is the negation of guidance in His saying, ﴿If only Allah had guided me﴾ [al-Zumar: 57]. Therefore the answer is (بلى), meaning: "No, rather We did guide you. ﴿My revelations did come to you, but you denied them﴾ [al-Zumar: 59]." The word (آيات) is the plural of (آية, ayah), which is a wondrous thing that catches the eye and calls the intellect and insight to reflection and contemplation.

As we have mentioned, the ayat are of three kinds. The first is the cosmic signs (kawniyyah), which show the power of the Creator, glory be to Him, as in His saying, ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, the sun and the moon﴾ [Fussilat: 37], and ﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty﴾ [al-Rum: 23].

These cosmic signs, which draw our attention to the Supreme Creator, are the first means to faith in Allah. Therefore, whenever the scholars deduce something new in the cosmos or discover something new, we find its origin in the Book of Allah, which the True One, glory be to Him, declared fourteen centuries ago.

The True One, glory be to Him, makes these cosmic signs manifest even through the hands of those who disbelieve in Him. Therefore, He warned against the scholars of the Sharia and the jurists interfering in the sciences of this world and the cosmos, because the cosmic sciences have scholars specialized in them. These scholars will serve the religion and the cause of faith in Allah, and they will show you the proofs and evidence for the obligation of believing in Allah, the Lord of this cosmos and its Creator.

So these scholars toil, reflect, and search in the cosmic sciences to serve the believer in Allah and to serve the religion. Even though they are disbelievers in Allah, they are soldiers of the Truth. And Allah the Exalted has spoken truly: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the Truth﴾ [Fussilat: 53].

Strangely, they will be deprived of reward for this effort they exerted, because they did it and reached what they reached while Allah, the True One, was not in their minds. Rather, serving humanity was in their minds. So let them take their wages from humanity. Indeed, humanity honored them, made statues for them, and celebrated them. Therefore, they have no share in the Hereafter.

The saying of Allah the Exalted applies to them: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan: 23].

And His saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing; and he finds Allah with him, and He pays him his account in full. And Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ [al-Nur: 39].

That is: he will be surprised to find that the cosmos has a Creator God, and he will be surprised by the reckoning and the recompense. These are matters that never crossed his mind in the world.

The second kind of ayat are the miracles that accompany the messages, to show the truthfulness of the Messenger in conveying what he receives from his Lord. Among them is His saying: ﴿And We gave Moses nine clear signs﴾ [al-Isra': 101].

As for the last kind, these are the Quranic verses that carry the rulings of the religion, and about which Allah said here: ﴿My revelations did come to you, but you denied them and became arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers﴾ [al-Zumar: 59].

His saying, ﴿and became arrogant﴾ [al-Zumar: 59], (استكبر, istakbara): it means he sought to be great. That is, he did not merely become arrogant; rather, he sought that and strove for it, but he was not granted it. This is because one who is arrogant must be independent of the one he is arrogant toward. And if you are in Allah's dominion and under His authority, eating from His provision and living in His goodness, then how can you be arrogant toward Him?

Furthermore, the arrogant person ought to be arrogant by means of something intrinsic in him that cannot be taken from him. Therefore, those who are arrogant in this world are only disputing with Allah His attribute, because they are arrogant without any capital. And which of the creatures possesses an essential quality that cannot be stripped from him? So we see that whoever is arrogant through honor, Allah humiliates him; whoever is arrogant through wealth, Allah impoverishes him; and whoever is arrogant through his health and well-being, Allah makes him ill.

Therefore, true arrogance is that you be proud of something you possess that cannot be taken from you. The worst of the arrogant is the one who is arrogant toward his Lord and Creator, who is capable of stripping him of everything. As for the one who is arrogant toward creatures, he is heedless of the greatness of his Lord and His majesty, because if he knew the greatness of his Lord and His majesty, he would be ashamed to be arrogant and to dispute with Allah one of His attributes.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 39, verse 60:

His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Those who lied against Allah﴾ [az-Zumar: 60], i.e., in their saying: ﴿If only Allah had guided me﴾ [az-Zumar: 57], and in other matters. For Allah guided you, showed you the way, and gave you direction when He sent you messengers supported by miracles, sent down the Books for you, and made clear to you the lawful and the unlawful. They lied in other matters as well, like those who said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 181], and like those who said: ﴿The hand of Allah is chained﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 64]. Similar to them are those who claimed that there are other gods with Allah.

All of these lied against Allah. Therefore, on the Day of Resurrection they will come ﴿with their faces blackened﴾ [az-Zumar: 60]. Yes, blackened, because they are now facing the truth that they lied about, so their faces must be blackened, with dust upon them and darkness covering them because of what they did.

This is not a condemnation of blackness in itself, for blackness is a creation among the creations of Allah and is not blameworthy in itself. You may see a man who is white in complexion, yet darkness and gloom overspread him, so you find his face dark, and we seek refuge in Allah. This is the effect of sins and wrongdoings upon the face in this world, before the Hereafter.

And you see a black-skinned servant whose face looks like a raisin, yet radiance and brightness shine over him, and you find on his face the signs of righteousness, as if his face gleams with light, and you never tire of looking at him. Therefore the Exalted says: ﴿Faces that Day will be bright, laughing, rejoicing. And faces that Day will have upon them dust, covered with darkness. Those are the disbelievers, the wicked﴾ [Abasa: 38–42].

So, the description is not praised or blamed in itself, and the blackness and whiteness here are not the blackness we know in this world; it is a relative matter. I used to see some of the righteous, as if in his face there was a lamp shining, and joy appeared upon his face, as if the light of certainty and the cheerfulness of faith had overflowed within him and spread over his face as light and freshness, and he had dark skin like ebony.

A similar matter is found in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the most hateful of voices is the voice of donkeys﴾ [Luqman: 19]. Is the voice of donkeys blamed when it comes from them? No, because the Creator made it in this form, and the loudness of the donkey's voice is for a wisdom: it may be hidden, for example, behind a mountain or a high hill, so that its owner cannot find it except through its voice. But loudness of voice is blamed in a human being, so he is the most hateful of voices if there comes from him something resembling the donkey's voice.

Likewise in: ﴿The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah, then did not carry it, is like the example of a donkey carrying books﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 5]. This is not a condemnation of the donkey, for the donkey in carrying performs a task, which is only carrying; it carries its load without complaint and without objection. But a human is blamed if he resembles the donkey, content for himself to carry only, without understanding what he carries, without comprehending, and without applying what he has learned.

As for His saying: ﴿Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the arrogant?﴾ [az-Zumar: 60], this is a negative interrogative to which we answer: "Yes, O Lord," meaning: No, rather they have a dwelling in Hell. The meaning is: what do they think? Do they think there is no place for them in it and no room? Rather, their place is ready and prepared with their names, awaiting them and longing for them. There is no housing shortage in Hell, as we have said.

Allah, the Exalted, created the creation from eternity, and assigned to each one of them a place in Paradise on the assumption that all of creation would believe in Allah, and assigned to each one of them a place in the Fire on the assumption that the creation would disbelieve. When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, the places of the people of the Fire that were prepared for them, had they believed, are distributed to the people of Paradise, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And that is the Paradise which you have been given as inheritance for what you used to do﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 72].

And the meaning of (مَثْوَى, mathwa, dwelling) is: a place of lodging and permanent residence for ﴿the arrogant﴾ [az-Zumar: 60].

This is the counterpart: the disbelievers have their abode and dwelling in Hell, while as for the believers, their Lord will deliver them ﴿with their salvation (bi-mafazatihim)﴾ [Az-Zumar: 61], meaning: with their success and their attainment of what they sought. The bliss of the Hereafter is attained in two ways: either a believer enters Paradise from the outset, or he is among the people of the Fire but the mercy of God overtakes him, so he is drawn away from it (yuzahzah) into Paradise.

As the Exalted says: ﴿Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has indeed succeeded﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 185]. Indeed, he has achieved the greatest success. For this reason, they call the deserts mafazah (a place of salvation), even though they are deadly, where the traveller may perish. Yet they named them mafazah out of optimism that the one who traverses them will come through safely. Likewise, they call the one stung by a serpent or a snake "al-saleem" (the safe one), hoping that he will be spared from its sting.

And if God delivers them and decrees for them success, they are safe from even the mere touch of punishment: ﴿Evil will not touch them, nor will they grieve﴾ [Az-Zumar: 61], because every scene they behold gladdens them, and nothing ever saddens them, as the Exalted says in another place: ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, [saying], "This is your Day, which you were promised"﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 103].

Having mentioned Allah's promise and warning, and having made clear the end of the disbelievers and the end of the believers, He returns to another matter of creed: ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾ [Az-Zumar: 62]. It is as if He is saying: what has turned them away from believing in Allah, the true God, when He is the Creator of all things?

Some people took this verse, ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾ [Az-Zumar: 62], and attributed all actions to Allah. In their view, Allah is the Creator of all things: the Creator of faith and the Creator of disbelief, the Creator of obedience and the Creator of disobedience. From this they said: then why does He punish the one who does it?

We say: there are those who are zealous for the power of the Truth and say, "everything is by His power, exalted is He." And there are those who are zealous for justice and say, "Man is the one who acts, and he is the one who strives for himself; therefore he is rewarded for obedience and punished for disobedience." This is a disagreement that should not have arisen among scholars, because obedience or disobedience is an act (fi'l), and what is the act?

The act is the performance by a limb of the body of its function. The eye sees, but the Creator, glory be to Him, set a law for sight and placed limits on it: the eye sees what is permitted to it and lowers its gaze from what is forbidden to it. Likewise the ear, the hand, the foot, and the tongue, and so on. If you conform in the act to the command of the Shari'ah (the revealed law), it is obedience; and if you contravene the command of the Shari'ah, it is disobedience.

For example, a man who raises his hand and strikes another. By Allah, is it he who made his limb act, or did he direct the limb toward what it is fit for? He is merely a director of the limb; otherwise he did not create the act in it. The proof is that he does not know the muscles that moved in him, nor the nerves that took part in this blow.

So we say: the act is one thing, and directing the limb toward the act is another thing. The whole act is created by Allah. He, glory be to Him, is the One who empowered the hands to strike, and He is the One who empowered them to extend good to others. The Creator, glory be to Him, is the One who enabled the tongue of the believer to say, "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," and enabled the tongue of the disbeliever to utter the word of disbelief, we seek refuge in Allah. With your eye you are able to look at what is lawful, and you are able to look with it at what is unlawful.

So: Allah has empowered every limb for the function it performs. If that function accords with the Shari'ah, it is obedience; and if it does not accord with it, it is disobedience. Accordingly we say: Allah, exalted is He, is truly the Creator of the act. So what did the servant do in disobedience that he should be punished for it? And what did he do in obedience that he should be rewarded for it?

The servant's act and his role here is only the directing of the energy which Allah created in him. This is the energy which Allah made fit to do a thing and its opposite. The capacity to act is not from you; it is from Allah, and it is upon you to direct the active energy.

So whoever looks at the act sees that the whole act belongs to Allah: ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾ [Az-Zumar: 62]. Whoever looks at the directing and the choice sees that it belongs to the servant. Therefore we say: the one who disobeys does not disobey against Allah by compulsion, and the disbeliever does not disbelieve outside the knowledge and will of Allah. For if the Truth, glory be to Him, had willed, He would have made all people one nation upon obedience and faith. But He left them choice and the directing of their acts, so that He, glory be to Him, who knows His servants best, might see who comes to Him willingly and by choice.

Therefore reflect upon His words, glory be to Him: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and were afraid of it; and man bore it. Indeed, he was ever unjust and ignorant﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 72].

It is therefore wrong to say that man alone is given choice. Rather, the whole universe is given choice before the Truth, glory be to Him. But the difference between the choice of the heavens and the earth and the choice of man is that when the heavens and the earth were given the choice, they chose to surrender their own desire to the desire of their Creator, glory be to Him. They chose in fact not to be choosers, and to be subdued to the will of their Lord. As for man, he accepted the Trust and chose to be one who chooses among multiple options.

We have previously explained the difference between bearing the Trust and performing the Trust: the servant may secure himself at the time of bearing it, but he cannot secure himself at the time of performing it. Thus it is a heavy matter, and for this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, described man in his bearing and his exposure to the Trust as unjust and ignorant.

So beware of entering a maze and understanding His words, exalted is He, ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾ [Az-Zumar: 62] in other than their proper sense, saying: He created the disbelief of the disbeliever and the disobedience of the disobedient, so why does He punish them? Because the disbeliever is the one who chose disbelief and directed the energy of Allah toward other than what Allah willed. The disobedient likewise directed the energy of Allah toward other than what Allah commanded.

Some say regarding ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾ [Az-Zumar: 62] that the universality here is relative, as in His words concerning the story of Bilqis: ﴿and she has been given of everything﴾ [An-Naml: 23]. That is, she was not given everything; the "min" here is partitive. The meaning, they say, is that they want to take the act of the servants out of this matter, and this is not permissible.

His words, exalted is He, ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾ [Az-Zumar: 62], are a report from the Truth, glory be to Him, which may bear more than one interpretation. But the evidences for the truth of this report arose even from those who disbelieve in Allah, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 87].

And He, glory be to Him and exalted, said: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [Luqman: 25].

So the container, the place, and the one who is contained are all the creation of Allah. Allah has reported this, and His Messenger (ﷺ) conveyed it. Among the people there were those who denied Allah and rejected Him and attributed partners to Him, yet none of them refuted this claim, and no one said, "I am the creator of this universe." A claim stands for its maker as long as no opposing evidence is raised against it. It is known that man claims what does not belong to him; had he possessed any part of creation, he would not have remained silent about it.

Then, man arose upon this universe, and found it as it is now, with its heaven and its earth. How then could he claim to be its creator, when he is more recent than it, and its creation is greater than his creation? ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know﴾ [Ghafir: 57].

So if a messenger came to us whose truthfulness we know, informing us that this universe has a Creator with such and such attributes, we would be obliged to lend him our ears so that we might hear the solution of this riddle. We illustrated this with a man who became stranded in a deadly desert until he neared death, and suddenly found a table laden with the finest food and drink. By Allah, what does he do before his hand reaches out to the food? He must ask himself: where did this table come from?

So: ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾ [Az-Zumar: 62] is a report for which there is evidence from existence itself, and evidence from those who oppose the Creator, glory be to Him. The truth is that they do not oppose the Truth over the matter of creation; rather they oppose Him by objecting to His law and His rulings, because these rulings will restrict their souls so that they cannot run wild in their desires. Faith carries obligations, and behind it lie accountability, punishment, and recompense. Otherwise, why did they worship idols?

They worshipped them because they are gods with no path and no obligations. They satisfy the innate disposition toward religiosity among them by having an object of worship, and how fine it is for that object of worship to have no command, no prohibition, and no obligations. So their saying: ﴿We only worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah in closeness﴾ [Az-Zumar: 3]: the word "worship" here is an erroneous term, because the meaning of worship is the worshipper's obedience to the command and prohibition of the one worshipped, and these idols have neither command nor prohibition.

His words, glory be to Him: ﴿and He is Disposer of all things﴾ [Az-Zumar: 62]. The wakīl (disposer, trustee) is the one you appoint to act on your behalf in a matter you cannot accomplish, as in the story of Prophet Musa (peace be upon him), when his people said to him: ﴿Indeed, we are to be overtaken﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 61]. At that moment they were right, because the sea was before them and Pharaoh and his soldiers were behind them; every indication supported their saying, ﴿Indeed, we are to be overtaken﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 61].

But Musa (peace be upon him) had another outlook and a different state. He was connected to his Lord, relying upon Him and entrusting himself to Him. He knew with certainty that Allah is his Trustee in what he is unable to do. Therefore he answered them and said, "No!" He did not say it from himself; he said it with the capital of his faith in his Lord and his confidence in His support: ﴿No! Indeed, my Lord is with me; He will guide me﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 62].

And He, exalted, says regarding reliance upon Him: ﴿Is He not who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him and removes the evil...?﴾ [An-Naml: 62].

And He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish except Him...﴾ [Al-Isra: 67]. So Allah is the Trustee of all His servants, including the disbeliever among them. Therefore we see that whoever disbelieves in Allah, when his means fail him or his affairs become constricted, says, "O Lord," because he does not deceive himself nor cheat himself.

Just as the Truth, glory be to Him, is truthful in reporting that He is ﴿the Creator of all things﴾ [Az-Zumar: 62], He is truthful in reporting that He is ﴿Disposer over all things﴾ [Az-Zumar: 62]. Do you not see, for example, the crop which the farmer plants and tends, so that you see it green and beautiful, but before the harvest a calamity sweeps over it or a blight strikes it and destroys it? By Allah, from whom is this blight? From your opponents and enemies? No... rather it is from Allah.

Since Allah, exalted is He, is the Creator of all things and the Disposer over all things, it is necessary that the dominion of the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. Therefore He said after it:

﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth...﴾.

The Qur'an is in clear Arabic, revealed in the Arabic dialects in use at the time of its revelation. Nevertheless, there are in the Qur'an words of Persian, Abyssinian or Greek (Roman) origin. These words do not take it out of being Arabic, because they had entered the language of the Arabs before the Qur'an was revealed; the Arab used them and knew them, and they became part of his language.

Among these words is (maqalid) in His saying: ﴿To Him belong the keys (maqalid) of the heavens and the earth﴾ [Az-Zumar: 63]. It is the plural of miqlad, on the pattern of miftah (key), or the plural of miqlid. In another dialect they say aqalid, the plural of iqlid. Its meaning is possession, disposal, preservation and safeguarding. So to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Him belongs absolute disposal of their affairs, and to Him, glorified is He, belongs their preservation and the management of their affairs.

This is the qayyumiyyah (the quality of self-subsisting sustainer) that belongs to Allah, the Exalted, by which every thing of His creation continues in its task. The Truth, glorified is He, created from non-existence, sustained what had been brought to nothing, legislated the laws and enacted the regulations. Then He did not leave creation to proceed by these laws alone, as some claim; rather He, glorified is He, stands over His creation as their Sustainer (Qayyum), never heedless of them for a single moment. Recite: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease. And if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him...﴾ [Fatir: 41].

If the universe proceeded by the laws that Allah created within it, as the philosophers say, then affairs would settle upon one unchanging state: the healthy would remain healthy, the mighty would remain mighty, and the wealthy would remain wealthy, and so on. But the matter is not so, because Allah has qayyumiyyah and disposal over His creation.

Our master Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, asked our master the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the keys (maqalid) of the heavens and the earth, and he said: "This is how the Messenger of Allah explained the phrase 'keys of the heavens and the earth': they are words of remembrance (dhikr)," as if the whole universe stands upon these doctrinal words.

The phrase "There is no god but Allah" means that Allah is One, with no partner. When He decrees a matter, no opponent opposes it and no objector objects to it. If He gives, no one can withhold His gift; and if He withholds, no one can give what He has withheld. Therefore He says: ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it﴾ [Al-Hajj: 73]. Rather, it is even less than the act of creation: ﴿And if the fly should steal from them a thing, they could not retrieve it from it﴾ [Al-Hajj: 73]. Can you recover from a fly what it has taken of honey, for example, if it lands on it? ﴿Weak are the seeker and the sought﴾ [Al-Hajj: 73].

Therefore this phrase, "There is no god but Allah," was spoken by the Truth, glorified is He, first, and He bore witness to it for Himself, glorified is He, with the witness of the Essence to the Essence. This witness means that nothing among creation can ever refuse Allah; therefore He says to a thing: "Be," and it is. Then the angels bore witness to it with the witness of direct observation; then those of knowledge bore witness to it with the witness of inference. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge, standing in justice﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18]. So the phrase "There is no god but Allah" is one of the keys (miqalid) that belong to Allah, the Exalted.

Likewise the phrase "Allahu Akbar" is one of the keys of the heavens and the earth. We have already explained that "Allahu Akbar" is our slogan in the call to prayer, although "Akbar" is not one of His names; rather, among His names is al-Kabir (the Great). So why did the call to prayer not use the name, but used the attribute "Akbar"?

We said: it is the superlative of kabir (great), because your Lord, when He calls you to prayer, removes you from the work of this world. This work is not trivial or insignificant; rather it is great and large, for by it the affairs of this world are established, and by it you are helped in the affairs of religion. So although it is great, Allah is greater. Leave the work for the prayer; as for the Name, al-Kabir, it is because all else is small.

The phrase "Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi" (Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him) is one of the keys of the heavens and the earth, because you will encounter matters beyond your comprehension that none can accomplish but Allah. So beware of standing before them to say, "How?" Rather, when an act is attributed to Allah, say: "Subhan Allah." We clarified this matter in the story of the Isra' (Night Journey); therefore it began with this phrase: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa﴾ [Al-Isra': 1].

There is no strangeness in this, because the act was attributed to Allah and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not say it. It is well known that an action is proportionate to its doer in strength and in time; if the doer is Allah, then no time is to be mentioned.

To illustrate this, we said: if you want to travel to Alexandria, for example, you may ride a donkey, a horse, a car, an airplane or a rocket. Would the time be the same? No, because the time is proportionate to the strength of the means; the greater the strength, the less the time. So if the doer of the Isra' is the Strength of all strengths, who is Allah, there is no doubt that the act requires no time.

When you contemplate the blood flowing in the arteries, it must have a certain degree of fluidity in order to flow. If this fluidity decreases, it clots and congeals in its channels, and may block the arteries so that a person dies. But when blood flows outside the body, it clots; while in the veins it remains fluid.

Consider the temperature of the body: the normal temperature is 37°C. Whether you live among the Eskimos or beside the equator, your temperature remains constant at 37°C. Nevertheless, within the human body there are organs whose temperatures differ while in the same body: the eye, for example, has a normal temperature of nine degrees, and the liver forty degrees. If the body's heat were to overcome the heat of the eye, a person would lose his sight.

It is well known that among the properties of heat or cold is the property of conduction (istitraq). How then would heat and cold not be conducted within the human body? These are all matters about which we must say: Glory be to Allah, Possessor of this power and its Originator.

Therefore: say "Subhan Allah" always in every astonishing matter. For this reason the Qur'an taught us this phrase for every act that none but Allah can accomplish. He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Glory be to He who took [His servant]﴾ [Al-Isra': 1], and He said: ﴿Glory be to He who created all the pairs from what the earth grows, and from themselves, and from that which they do not know﴾ [Ya-Sin: 36].

The phrase "Subhan Allah" should be joined with His praise, glorified is He, as if you were praising Allah that He is exalted above resembling creation or being like creation. Praise belongs to Allah: He has no likeness, no equal, and no rival, because the fruit of this declaration of His transcendence returns to you yourself, O believer.

The phrase "Astaghfir Allah al-'Azim" (I seek forgiveness from Allah, the Mighty) is one of the keys of the heavens and the earth. If you are heedless of Me, then it is among My keys that I forgive you if you seek forgiveness, so that I do not deprive you of repentance and turning back to Me. And the forgiveness of this world is the erasure of sin; it is a manifestation of His mercy toward us, because if the door of repentance were closed in the face of the servant, he would rage in disobedience and persist in transgressing against others.

Therefore: the legislation of repentance has spared mankind from the evils of mankind.

The phrase "La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah" (There is no might nor power except through Allah) is also one of the keys of the heavens and the earth. When you set about something, beware of thinking that you undertake it by your own strength and power; rather, you have no might and no power except through Allah, for it is He, glorified is He, who is able to strip you of might and to strip you of power.

Have you not reflected on your hand... how you move it however you wish, with ease and smoothness, while it obeys you and submits to you, and you do not even know the muscles and nerves that take part in this movement, nor are you aware of them?

It is the power of Allah in you. If He, glorified is He, wishes to strip you of this strength, He withholds the electrical impulse coming from the brain to this organ, and you try to lift it and cannot. Therefore: keep this matter always in mind whenever you set about an act, and know that it is not accomplished by your strength but by the strength of Allah.

The phrase "He is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward" is one of the keys of the heavens and the earth. He, glorified is He, is the First without beginning and the Last without end, as we said in the Ramadan supplication: "O First, with no before; O Last, with no after; but that is within that; so stand, O intellect, at your limit."

The meaning of "the Outward" is that which is outwardly manifest within Allah's dominion, which falls under the perception of sight; and "the Inward" is that which is hidden in the malakut (unseen realm) of Allah, which you do not see. Allah, the Exalted, has an apparent dominion and an unapparent malakut, which none is informed of except whom He wills among His servants, at the time He wishes, glorified is He.

The phrase "In His hand is the good" is also one of the keys. Some scholars said: "In His hand is the good and the evil," looking at His saying: ﴿Say: O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You remove sovereignty from whom You will. You honour whom You will and You degrade whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Indeed, You are over all things competent﴾ [Al 'Imran: 26].

When the verse combined a thing and its opposite, it emboldened them to say "in His hand is the good and the evil," and this is not permissible. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "In His hand is the good," out of courtesy toward Allah, and did not attribute evil to Allah. We likewise do not attribute evil to Allah, the Exalted. Therefore, since 1928 I have objected to our saying in supplication: "And protect us from the evil of what You have decreed," and I said: this supplication must be amended. Then the Truth, glorified is He, guided us to its solution, and we said: the evil of what You decree is that you are not content with the decree.

If we reflect on the phrase "In His hand is the good" and on the verse ﴿In Your hand is all good﴾ [Al 'Imran: 26], we find that "the good" here is absolute, meaning that all the actions of the Truth, glorified is He, are good, and evil comes only from creation. Recite: ﴿Whatever good reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil reaches you is from yourself﴾ [An-Nisa': 79].

If you say: how do we reconcile a verse like this with His saying: ﴿Say: All is from Allah﴾ [An-Nisa': 78]? We say: we have already clarified the solution to this riddle. Yes, all is from Allah, meaning that Allah, the Exalted, is the Creator of the act, that is, the Creator of the power and capacity by which one acts. But you direct this capacity either toward good or toward evil. Accordingly we say: the good is from Allah and the evil is from us.

His saying "He gives life and causes death" is also one of the keys. Death and life are the first phenomenon in human existence, and the Creator, glorified is He, created both life and death. When He spoke to us about this, He, the Exalted, said: ﴿He who created death and life to test you as to which of you is best in deed, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving﴾ [Al-Mulk: 2].

He mentioned death first, so that we do not receive life with the delusion of permanence; rather we receive it with the awareness in our minds that we will end in death, so that we work for this end. ﴿And He is over all things competent﴾ [Ar-Rum: 50], meaning: He does what you are unable to do. He, glorified is He, has absolute power, so nothing overpowers Him and nothing is beyond Him. Therefore, when you ask your Lord for provision, ask that He provide for you from where you do not expect, for Allah has means of provision that you do not know. That is why the people of knowledge said: "The means are a veil over the hand of Allah in giving."

So His saying, the Exalted, ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾ [Az-Zumar: 63] means: by His creative power and His constant qayyumiyyah. ﴿And those who disbelieved in the signs of Allah﴾ [Az-Zumar: 63], whether they are cosmic signs, the miracles of messengers, or the verses of the Book bearing the rulings. To disbelieve in them means to be arrogant toward carrying them out. ﴿Those are the losers﴾ [Az-Zumar: 63], meaning their transaction is ruinous and their trade is ruined, because they preferred the immediate desire over the lasting bliss that will not escape you nor you it.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Say, "Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship...?"﴾.

Remember what the disbelievers of Makkah did: they opposed the Messenger of Allah, confronted him, and refused the religion of Allah. Despite this, Islam spread and its followers increased, so the disbelievers tried to reach a compromise with the Messenger of Allah. They said to him: "O Muhammad, you worship our gods for a year, and we will worship your God for a year." So Allah responded to them. (Say) O Muhammad, in reply to them: ﴿Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?﴾ [al-Zumar: 64]. The interrogative here expresses astonishment and denial: do you want me, though I am the Messenger of Allah and His trustee over His revelation and His message, to worship other than Him?

Regarding the word (ta'murūnnī) (you order me), several readings have been transmitted: ta'murūnnī with a doubled nūn, and ta'murūnanī, and the nūn here is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāyah), meaning it protects the verb from being given a kasrah; and ta'murūnī with a single yā'.

The word (a'budu) (I worship) originally was an an a'buda; when (an) was deleted, the verb took its natural form with a ḍammah (raf'). This word indicates that worshipping idols, or worshipping other than Allah, is fundamentally invalid in reason, because worship, as we have mentioned, is the obedience of the worshipper to the one worshipped, and idols have no method that we could obey or disobey.

Therefore He described their worshippers as ignorant: ﴿O ignorant ones﴾ [al-Zumar: 64]. We must distinguish between the jāhil (ignorant person) and the ummī (unlettered person): the ummī is better than the jāhil, because his mind is empty and he holds no proposition he clings to, so it is easy for you to convince him. As for the jāhil, his mind is not empty; rather he has a mistaken proposition that contradicts reality and he clings to it, so he needs redoubled effort: first to remove the mistaken proposition from him, and then to place the correct proposition in him.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾ [al-Ahzab: 4].

We have previously discussed the matter of the ḥayyiz (space), that a single space can contain only one thing. So, for example, when we fill a jug with water, air bubbles come out first before the water enters; similarly, the corrupt proposition in the heart of the ignorant person must come out first before he accepts the truth, and the more the proposition agrees with his desire, the harder its removal, and from here the ignorant person is more difficult for the teacher than the unlettered one.

This matter of the ḥayyiz is an innate principle that the philosopher, the child, and the shepherd all arrive at. Do you not see that a small child sits, for example, beside his father, and if his brother wants to sit in his place, he stands up for him and seats him? Why? Because he knows this principle: that one place can hold only one thing.

So: the disbelievers were described as ignorant because they believe in a mistaken proposition and cling to it, and it is hard to dislodge them from it, which is the proposition of associating partners with Allah. And what ignorance is greater than worshipping idols?

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And it has certainly been revealed to you and to those before you...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 39, verse 65:

This verse explains the reason for the interrogation and the expression of astonishment in: ﴿Will you then order me to worship other than Allah, O you ignorant ones?﴾ [al-Zumar: 64]. That is: how do you order me to do that, when I am the Messenger entrusted with the religion and the revelation, and Allah has revealed to me and to those before me: ﴿If you were to associate partners with Allah, your deeds would surely be nullified, and you would surely be among the losers﴾ [al-Zumar: 65]. This is the reason for their being called ignorant, in their saying to the Messenger of Allah: "We worship your God for a year, and you worship our gods for a year."

The meaning of ﴿And to those before you﴾ [al-Zumar: 65] is: the earlier Messengers, because each of them was addressed with this same matter. But can it be conceived of the Messengers that they would associate partners with Allah? They said: this is a hypothetical supposition (fard); that is, if we suppose that, then this would be their recompense. It is similar to the saying (I mean you, but listen, O neighbour). So if this threat is directed at the Messengers, it is directed all the more so at the common people.

Some scholars said regarding this verse, ﴿And it has certainly been revealed to you and to those before you﴾ [al-Zumar: 65]: you are speaking here about the infallibility (ʿișma) of the Messengers, but this infallibility is by the decree of Allah, and the decree of Allah no one possesses. Did not a Messenger among the Messengers say: ﴿We would have fabricated a lie against Allah if we returned to your religion after Allah has rescued us from it. It would not be for us to return to it unless Allah, our Lord, should will. Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge..﴾ [al-A'raf: 89].

The meaning is that He has given power the freedom to do what it wills, even though this does not happen.

The content of the revelation to you and to those before you is: ﴿If you associate partners with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified﴾ [al-Zumar: 65]. However, the verse places those to whom revelation was sent on one side, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the other side. Allah addressed His Messenger specifically in ﴿If you associate partners﴾ [al-Zumar: 65], and the address to the Messenger of Allah indicates that it is directed also to the earlier Messengers.

The meaning of ﴿your deeds will surely be nullified﴾ [al-Zumar: 65] is: they will be corrupted and lost, to no benefit. ﴿And you will surely be among the losers﴾ [al-Zumar: 65]. We know in trade that loss means that the capital itself decreases. So the merchant who does not make a profit over his capital is not called a loser, as long as his capital remains intact for him.

Likewise the believer: his capital in his trade with Allah is his faith and his righteous deeds. Your Lord created you from nothing and sustained you from non-existence, sent Messengers to you and sent down Books for you, and thereby made for you a profitable transaction with Him, glory be to Him. And it is incumbent upon you, O believer, to seize this opportunity to profit with Allah, because the deed you do in this world is a deed limited by your life and your lifespan in this world.

As for the reward for deeds, it is in the Hereafter, which is not limited but lasting and enduring, and herein lies the distinction of trade with Allah. Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And indeed, the Last Abode—that is the [true] life, if they only knew﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 64].

The word "bal" (بل) is a particle that expresses turning away from the preceding speech and affirming what follows. The meaning is: turn away from their invitation that you worship their gods, and beware of inclining toward them. ﴿Rather, worship Allah﴾ [Az-Zumar: 66]. To emphasize the worship of Allah alone, the verse is phrased this way: "bal Allaha fa'bud" (rather, Allah, so worship), placing the object before the verb. This is called the style of restriction (qasr), meaning the restriction of worship to Allah alone, to the exclusion of anyone else, as in His saying: ﴿You alone do we worship﴾ [Al-Fatihah: 5].

Placing the detached pronoun referring to the Truth (al-Haqq), subhanahu, before the verb "na'bud" (we worship) means: we worship You alone, not anyone other than You. Had we said "na'budu-ka" (we worship You), it could imply that we also worship others. His saying: ﴿and be among the thankful﴾ [Az-Zumar: 66] means: be among those who thank Allah for guidance and success, by worshipping Him alone and giving thanks for the blessings He has already bestowed upon you. These blessings are only an "urbun" (down payment, earnest) for the everlasting bliss that awaits you.

Among the marvels of Allah's gentleness toward us (lutf) is that He has legislated for us commands and prohibitions in which lies our good in this world, and then rewards us for them in the Hereafter if we obey, and warns us of punishment if we disobey. He, glorified is He, is gentle with us and eager for our salvation, although He gains nothing from that at all: no obedience benefits Him, and no disobedience harms Him.

Consider the sacred hadith (hadith qudsi) on the lips of the Lord of Might, glorified is He: "Know, O servant, that your Lord loves you and desires for you success and salvation, for you are His servant and His creation, and the maker desires for his creation to be in the best of states."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 39, verse 67:

The meaning of ﴿وَمَا قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ﴾ [al-Zumar: 67] is: they did not measure Allah by His true measure, nor did they magnify Him with the magnificence fitting to Him, glorified is He. That is, they did not know Allah's worth, and for this reason they associated partners with Him. Shirk in itself is the failure to measure Allah by His true measure. They did this while ﴿the earth entirely will be His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand﴾ [al-Zumar: 67]. So: how could this happen from you? Have you overlooked this reality? You will surely see the outcome of your deed in the Hereafter.

As for the meaning of ﴿the earth entirely will be His grip on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Zumar: 67], we say: "This matter is in my hands," meaning: I have full control over it, such that it cannot escape from me. It is not necessary with regard to God, exalted is He, that there be in the matter a grip or a hand. Here it is a metaphor (kinaya) for power and control, just as we say, for example, "We have seized the criminal," meaning: he has come into our possession and is no longer free in life to do as he pleases.

We have already said: when an attribute is mentioned for the Real (al-Haqq), glorified is He, that has a likeness among His servants, then take it within the framework of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura: 11]. Among this are the attributes of hearing, sight, hand, and knowledge, etc.

The word ﴿the earth entirely﴾ [al-Zumar: 67] refers to our earth on which we live and to similar earths, because Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾ [al-Talaq: 12]. This is all within our solar system. So what of the rest of the systems and galaxies that contain millions like our earth: ﴿And He is, over their gathering when He wills, competent﴾ [al-Shura: 29].

As for His saying ﴿and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand﴾ [al-Zumar: 67], it means He folds them by His power, exalted is He. The right hand (al-yamin), in our understanding, is the one that acts upon things and is the source of strength. Therefore He, glorified is He, said: ﴿You used to come to us from the right﴾ [al-Saffat: 28], that is, from the direction of strength. In another place, the Real, glorified is He and exalted, said: ﴿The Day We will roll up the heaven like the rolling of the recorded scrolls. As We originated the first creation, We will repeat it﴾ [al-Anbiya: 104].

But what earth do we mean in His saying ﴿the earth entirely will be His grip on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Zumar: 67]? They said: it is an earth other than the earth we know, because the earth will be changed in the Hereafter, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿The Day the earth will be changed to another earth, and the heavens﴾ [Ibrahim: 48]. The earth of this world is an earth of means (asbab), on which we live, eat from its fruit, and carry on our lives; but in the Hereafter, life there is through the Causer (al-Musabbib), glorified is He.

The earth of the Hereafter has no planting, no ploughing, and no harvesting. Rather, one eats and drinks merely by the will to eat or drink. Whatever you think of, you find before you, not by means but by the power of the Causer, glorified is He. Likewise, the sky in this world is a sky of means, from which rain descends, in which the sun shines, and which the moon illuminates. In the Hereafter, however, there is none of that: no rain, no sun, and no moon; rather, the earth is illuminated by the light of its Lord.

As for His saying, exalted is He, at the close of this verse ﴿Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate﴾ [al-Zumar: 67], it is a command that we say "Glory be to Allah" and that we declare Him free of resemblance to His creation in the matter of the grip and in the folding of the heavens, because it is not like the folding that we know. Rather, these attributes should be taken within the framework of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura: 11]. So Allah is exalted above what the polytheists say.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 39, verse 68:

After the Almighty had spoken of the beliefs, and mentioned the promise to the obedient and the warning to the disobedient, He willed to tell us about the Hereafter, which is the abode of recompense for deeds done in this world. In this world there are the dead and there are the living, and the Hour will not arise unless everyone has died, so that resurrection may be realized; otherwise, how could resurrection apply to one who has not died? For this reason the Almighty tells us here about the blowing of the Trumpet (al-Sur), this blast which causes death for everyone who is alive.

The verb (nufikha, "was blown") is in the passive voice, its subject not named, but the Sunnah has made clear the agent, that he is Israfil. And (al-Sur) is a horn like a waterskin, into which Israfil blows the first blast, which causes the death of all the living, because the Resurrection will arise while on the earth there are living beings who must die, so that there may be a resurrection for them, like those who died from the time of Adam, peace be upon him, until the Hour arises.

And the Almighty says: ﴿Every soul shall taste death﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 57].

But: is the first blast the one that causes death, or is the second blast the one that gives life to the dead?

We say: the blast itself neither gives life nor causes death; rather, it is a notice to the One who holds the matter that He should begin His work: ﴿And whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon﴾ [al-Zumar: 67]. The word (sa'iqa, "swooned/died") comes with two meanings.

Sa'iqa in the sense of "perished", as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿So leave them until they meet their Day in which they will be struck senseless﴾ [al-Tur: 45], meaning: they will perish.

And sa'iqa comes in the sense of "fainted, losing consciousness", as happened to our master Musa, peace be upon him, when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain. When Musa called upon his Lord he said: ﴿My Lord, show me Yourself that I may look upon You. He said: You will not see Me﴾ [al-A'raf: 143]. The meaning here is not that I cannot be seen; rather, I can be seen, but in your present constitution you cannot see Me. Thus the condition may change into a form in which you are able to see Me.

And if mankind has reached methods, means and causes by which they can see what they were unable to see before, as we have seen with spectacles, magnifying spectacles and telescopes, etc., then the Almighty is, by greater right, able to make you see what you did not used to see before.

Then the Almighty says, completing this story: ﴿But look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me﴾ [al-A'raf: 143]. The Almighty wishes to confirm this matter to Musa, peace be upon him, not by saying but by deed: ﴿When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, and Musa fell down swooning﴾ [al-A'raf: 143].

It is as if the Almighty is saying to His prophet Musa: if you swooned, that is, lost consciousness, from seeing the one manifested upon, which is the mountain, then how will it be with you when you see the One who manifests Himself, glorified is He?

And His saying ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾ [al-Zumar: 68] means: He willed that they not swoon. This exemption is temporary, since whoever did not die in this first blast must die afterwards; the last to die will be the Angel of Death, to whom the Almighty says: "Die, O Angel of Death", and he dies. After that, immortality without end.

They have said: those whom Allah excepted from this blast are the angels entrusted (with tasks): Jibril, Mika'il, 'Azra'il and Israfil. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, informed us that Musa, peace be upon him, is among those excepted from this swoon. For it is reported in the hadith that the swoon occurred and the people were struck with a fainting; the Messenger of Allah was the first to regain consciousness from it and he found his brother Musa, peace be upon them both, holding onto the Throne. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not know whether Musa had been swooned among those who swooned and regained consciousness before me, or whether he had not been swooned.

Since he regained consciousness and found Musa beside the Throne, then he was not swooned, and he is among those whom Allah excepted in His saying ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾ [al-Zumar: 68]; or else he was swooned but regained consciousness from the swoon before others. Here the scholars said: why was Musa, peace be upon him, not swooned, or why was the duration of his swoon shorter than that of the others? They said: because he, peace be upon him, had previously been struck in this world when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, so Allah willed that this swoon be counted for him and that the swoon of the Resurrection be lightened for him.

And His saying ﴿Then it will be blown again﴾ [al-Zumar: 68] means: the blast of resurrection. The first blast caused the death of those who had not yet died, and the second blast is the resurrection and the coming forth from the graves: ﴿and at once they will be out of the graves hastening to their Lord﴾ [Ya-Sin: 51]. This is a depiction of the state of the swoon and of the manner of emerging from the graves: ﴿Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on﴾ [al-Zumar: 68].

The word (yansilun, "hastening") indicates dispersal after gathering, as we say of cloth "nassil", meaning that after its threads were tightly joined, they have come apart. This is a precise depiction and an eloquent expression portraying the state that existed in the graves when the dead meet in the depths of the earth, because people in this world, while in the abundance of life, constantly quarrel and fight, and enmities and rivalries multiply among them.

The poet expressed this meaning when he said:

How many a tomb has become a tomb many times, laughing at the crowding of opposites.

When they die and the earth gathers them, it absorbs whatever resentments and enmities were between them, and their elements become so pure that it enables them to meet and gather, so they say: how sweet is the embrace before the knocks of separation.

It is as if they rejoice in this gathering and this embrace, because it compensates them for the discord that was between them in this world. Then when the second blast comes, this gathering comes apart and disperses. This is the meaning of ﴿yansilun﴾ [Ya-Sin: 51]: each one alone, by himself and in his own person, as a thread comes out of its place in the weave; that is because recompense is a personal matter and each is held in pledge by his deed.

The meaning of ﴿yanzurun﴾ [al-Zumar: 68] is: they wait for what will befall them, or they look at what is around them of terrors at which the eyes stare, as He says in another verse, relating their words: ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and we have heard﴾ [al-Sajda: 12]. They have said: this is the only verse in which sight is placed before hearing. Why? Because the situation here, in the Hereafter, is when people are raised from the graves, and when terrors and distresses surround them from every side, and in this state sight precedes hearing, so they see before they hear.

With the blast of resurrection the terrors of the Hour begin and the distress grows heavy on the disbelievers, so they tremble. Then when Allah makes true His promise and His warning about the arising of the Hour in its first stage, at that point they will know the truth of what they denied and disbelieved in, those who had so often denied resurrection and said: ﴿Are we indeed to be raised, we and our forefathers of old?﴾ [al-Saffat: 16–17].

So: Allah has spoken truly about resurrection and the bringing back of the dead, and He will speak truly concerning what follows of reckoning and recompense; and woe to you, disbelievers who deny.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 39, verses 69–70:

This verse transports us to another world, to the Hereafter, where the earth is changed into a different earth and the heavens into different heavens. In this world we live on the earth by the light of the sun, and we say: "The sun has risen." But once we have moved to the Hereafter, the earth itself shines: ﴿And the earth shall shine with the light of its Lord..﴾ [al-Zumar: 69], as though light were an intrinsic attribute of it, so that there is no sun shining upon it; rather, it is the one that shines by its own essence.

And why not? You are now in a world in which "no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived" (hadith qudsi, as it is commonly cited). God, the Exalted, says: ﴿They will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold﴾ [al-Insan: 13], because the world was run by means (asbab), so the sun shines to illuminate the earth by day and the moon by night. In the Hereafter, however, we do not live by means, but by the One who causes them (al-musabbib), subhanahu, where everything happens there without any treatment. Therefore we have no need to cultivate the earth, nor for the sun to light the day, nor for the moon to light the night.

Just as the earth is changed into a different earth, and the heavens into different heavens, so you too will be changed into another form suited to the Hereafter: you will eat but will not defecate, and you will live but will not grow old.

When the earth shines with the light of its Lord, you see it shining without seeing the source of this radiance. We have seen something of this in this world: in modern lighting methods, lamps are placed in positions that hide the source of light, so the light comes indirectly and does not harm the eye, just as sunlight comes and lights the room for you while you do not see the direct ray of the sun.

God, the Truthful, has also given us an example of His illuminating the heavens and the earth, in Surat al-Nur, where He, subhanahu, says: ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth..﴾ [al-Nur: 35], i.e., the One who illuminates them. And when He wished to give us an example of this, He brought an example from what is visible to us and perceptible, saying: ﴿The likeness of His light is like a niche in which is a lamp..﴾ [al-Nur: 35], i.e., the manner of His illumination and the effect of His light, lest we think that this example clarifies to us the light of God. Rather, it clarifies the manner of His illuminating His creation; otherwise His light, exalted be He, we do not know its reality nor perceive its essence.

The mishkah (niche) is the non-penetrating recess in the wall, which they call a kuwwah (alcove), and such recesses still exist in old traditional buildings. The mishkah is where the lamp is placed, and it is not the lamp itself, as superficial people suppose when they use it in this sense. The feature of the mishkah is that it is non-penetrating and limited in area, so that it gathers the light of the lamp and it does not disperse, but concentrates to illuminate the room in which this mishkah is located.

Then He describes the lamp as not an ordinary lamp, but ﴿a lamp within a glass..﴾ [al-Nur: 35]. The glass purifies the light of the lamp and prevents excess air from reaching it, so that no smoke arises to cloud the clarity and purity of the light.

Then this glass is also not ordinary, but ﴿the glass is as if it were a brilliant star..﴾ [al-Nur: 35]. The "brilliant star" (kawkab durri) is that which shines by itself, and this means that the light of this lamp is doubled.

Then the oil with which the lamp is lit is not ordinary oil, but oil taken from a tree of moderate temperament: ﴿lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it; light upon light..﴾ [al-Nur: 35].

Some object to this example and say: How does God give an example of His light by a niche in which there is a lamp? We say: The example here is not an example of God's light, but an example of His illumination of the cosmos. The poet Abu Tammam expressed this meaning in his saying, praising:

The boldness of ʿAmr with the generosity of Hatim, with the forbearance of al-Ahnaf and the intelligence of Iyas.

One of the patron's companions objected to him and said: How do you equate the prince with the boors of the Arabs? The prince is above whom you have described. Abu Tammam, after lowering his head for a moment, replied:

Do not deny my striking an example for him with one lesser than him,
unique in generosity and valour,

For God has struck the lesser example for His light, a likeness of the niche and the lamp-wick.

Thus God illuminates for creation the sensible light that protects their substance and preserves the soundness of their movement in life, for if a person walks without guidance he collides with the things around him, and collision means that the strong crushes the weak. Therefore we take care to have a dim light (wasina) at night, for example, to protect our movement from collision.

If the Creator, subhanahu, has made for us sensible light to protect our substance from being broken or breaking, then He must make for us a spiritual light that protects values within us, so that we do not destroy by injustice, nor destroy by oppression. This is the light of revelation and the Law, by which hearts live and which organises our spiritual movement on the journey of life.

Just as God, the Truthful, has explained to us the sensible light, He has explained to us the spiritual light, saying: take it from the houses of God. He, exalted, says: ﴿In houses which God has permitted to be raised and in which His name is mentioned; glorifying Him therein in the mornings and the evenings. Men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of God and the establishment of prayer and the giving of zakat, fearing a Day when hearts and eyes will be overturned..﴾ [al-Nur: 36–37].

So: take the spiritual light from the houses of God, for there you meet God, the Exalted. This meeting bestows upon you a light from the light of God that fills your heart, guides your limbs and sets you right. God, subhanahu, has shown that the light of values is higher than the light of matter, as evidenced by the fact that a person who is blind can walk and carry on his affairs in this world, whereas one who lacks spiritual light, or who is "blind of insight" as they say, can never be guided to rightness in his movement. Therefore, at the end of the verse, He, exalted, said: ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth..﴾ [al-Nur: 35], then said: ﴿Light upon light; God guides to His light whom He wills..﴾ [al-Nur: 35].

After the earth has shone with the light of its Lord, ﴿and the Book is placed..﴾ [al-Zumar: 69]. In another place the detail and explanation of this came, where God, subhanahu, says: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is within it, and they will say: "Woe to us! What sort of book is this that leaves nothing small or great but has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present, and your Lord does not wrong anyone.﴾ [al-Kahf: 49].

Thus God explained what was summarised in ﴿and the Book is placed..﴾ [al-Zumar: 69]. It is well known that the verses of the Noble Qur'an explain one another. The Book here is a book specific to each person individually, as God, subhanahu, says: ﴿And every person We have fastened his bird (deeds) to his neck, and We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a book he will find spread open. "Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as an accountant."﴾ [al-Isra: 13–14].

This book that records your deeds is a book of truth, because its writer is an angel appointed over you: ﴿noble recorders, who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar: 11–12], and He says: ﴿Not a word does he utter but that with him is an observer, ready.﴾ [Qaf: 18].

This book is not merely in God's knowledge, for God's knowledge is speech from Him; rather, this is a book in the sense that it is written and readable, which its owner reads and looks upon, seeing in it his righteous and wicked deeds. Therefore, when the criminals see it they tremble with fear, because it has counted their crimes and left out nothing, small or great; then they can only call upon themselves for woe and destruction.

After each takes his book, God brings the prophets: ﴿and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought..﴾ [al-Zumar: 69], so that every prophet may testify that he conveyed to his community. He, exalted, says: ﴿On the Day when God gathers the messengers and says: "What response were you given?"..﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 109].

After the messengers testify, the witnesses testify, namely those who bore knowledge after the messengers, as it is related: "This knowledge is carried by the upright of every generation, who expel from it the distortion of the extremists, the false claims of the falsifiers, and the interpretation of the ignorant."

These scholars too testify that they conveyed to others. Therefore the community of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is distinguished by its scholars, because they are an extension of his message, may God bless him and grant him peace. Thus our excellence over the nations lies in this matter.

The martyrs who were slain in the way of God also testify, and they too testify to their station with God, a station they attained through martyrdom. It is enough that the martyr enters the battle knowing that if he is defeated he will be killed; he advances either for victory or for martyrdom. He knows he will give up his life as a price, and had he not been fully confident in what God promised him of reward, he would not have gone out.

Therefore God said about the martyrs: ﴿And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of God as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 169].

It is strange to hear someone say, in denial: "So if we took the martyr out of his grave, would we find him alive?" We say: Read the verse and reflect on its meaning. God says: ﴿alive with their Lord..﴾ [Al 'Imran: 169], not with you, as is shown by the fact that it is followed by the verb of provision for life, saying: "being provided for" (yurzaqun). That is because when the martyr sacrificed his life, his Lord guaranteed him another life, better, greater and more enduring than what he had in this world. Therefore the poet said about our master Hamzah, the master of the martyrs:

O Hamzah, uncle of the Chosen One, you are a master
over all the martyrs of the earth, all of them.

And enough for you of that martyrdom is a protection from death, the life connected to the other.

The meaning: you offered your life and sacrificed it, so you were protected from death, because after you died you became alive, and your life in this world was connected to your life in the Hereafter; you gave life, so life was joined.

The testimony against the servant on the Day of Resurrection does not end at this point. After the angels have testified against him by the book they wrote, and the prophets and martyrs have testified against him, we move the testimony to your very self: this is a gradation in testimony, from the angels, who are of a kind other than yours, to the prophets and martyrs, who are of your kind, to your limbs, which are a part of you: ﴿Today We shall seal upon their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn.﴾ [Ya Sin: 65].

And He, subhanahu, says: ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will testify against them to what they used to do.﴾ [al-Nur: 24].

And God, exalted, says: ﴿Until, when they reach it, their hearing, their eyes and their skins will testify against them to what they used to do. And they will say to their skins: "Why did you testify against us?" They will say: "God has made us speak, who makes everything speak; and He created you the first time, and to Him you are returned."﴾ [Fussilat: 20–21].

The tongue is what spoke, the hand is what seized, and the foot is what walked... etc.? They said: Because God created the limbs for His servant and subjected them to His purpose, and commanded them to obey him in what he wills. The tongue is subjected to serve its owner: if he wishes to say "There is no god but God," he says it; and if he wishes to utter a word of disbelief, he utters it. And likewise the remaining limbs.

So: as long as the human being is in this world, authority over the limbs belongs to the will of the choosing human, and the limbs follow his will. But when we are resurrected and presented before the Creator, subhanahu, this will is dissolved and taken away, and no will belongs to anyone except God: ﴿"To whom belongs the dominion this Day? To God, the One, the Subduer."﴾ [Ghafir: 16]. Then the limbs are freed and stand in the position of a truthful witness.

And God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and they will not be wronged.﴾ [al-Zumar: 69], i.e., God judges between the people and the people of the gathering, and decides among the creatures, and the one who judges is God. Therefore it is a judgement by truth in which no one is wronged. No one has a will on this day, and no one has a decision or a desire; the whole matter belongs to God. If He wills, He exacts retribution for the wronged from the wrongdoer, and if He wills, He pleases the wronged and pardons the wrongdoer.

Then He, subhanahu, says: ﴿And every soul will be paid in full what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do.﴾ [al-Zumar: 70], i.e., He recompenses it for what it did: if good, then good; if evil, then evil.

Orientalists have stopped at this verse, claiming that its context lacks coherence. Coherence in their view would be to say: "And every soul is paid in full what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do." They say this because they do not grasp the difference between fi'l (act) and 'amal (deed). Fi'l is the opposite of qawl (speech): the tongue alone has the task of speech, while the rest of the limbs act; the eye sees, the ear hears, the hand seizes, the foot strides... etc.

Every limb has its function, and these are all acts (af'al). But 'amal encompasses both speech and act, and each of them is called 'amal. Therefore God says: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ [al-Saff: 2].

But why did He single out the tongue for the first portion and the other limbs for the other portion? They said: Because speech is the means of conveyance and transmission, so it deserved to be the foremost of the limbs.

What is the result of this full payment of deeds? The result of the full payment of deeds is that every soul receives what it deserves for its deeds in this world. Therefore, after the payment is complete and the reckoning is done, the people of faith are driven to Paradise, and the people of disbelief are driven to Hell:

﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups...﴾.

Therefore we have no need to cultivate the earth, nor for the sun to light the day, nor for the moon to light the night.

Just as the earth is changed into a different earth, and the heavens into different heavens, so you too will be changed into another form suited to the Hereafter: you will eat but will not defecate, and you will live but will not grow old.

When the earth shines with the light of its Lord, you see it shining without seeing the source of this radiance. We have seen something of this in this world: in modern lighting methods, lamps are placed in positions that hide the source of light, so the light comes indirectly and does not harm the eye, just as sunlight comes and lights the room for you while you do not see the direct ray of the sun.

And when He wished to give us an example of this, He brought an example from what is visible to us and perceptible, saying: ﴿The likeness of His light is like a niche in which is a lamp..﴾ [al-Nur: 35], i.e., the manner of His illumination and the effect of His light, lest we think that this example clarifies to us the light of God. Rather, it clarifies the manner of His illuminating His creation; otherwise His light, exalted be He, we do not know its reality nor perceive its essence.

The mishkah (niche) is the non-penetrating recess in the wall, which they call a kuwwah (alcove), and such recesses still exist in old traditional buildings. The mishkah is where the lamp is placed, and it is not the lamp itself, as superficial people suppose when they use it in this sense. The feature of the mishkah is that it is non-penetrating and limited in area, so that it gathers the light of the lamp and it does not disperse, but concentrates to illuminate the room in which this mishkah is located.

Then He describes the lamp as not an ordinary lamp, but ﴿a lamp within a glass..﴾ [al-Nur: 35]. The glass purifies the light of the lamp and prevents excess air from reaching it, so that no smoke arises to cloud the clarity and purity of the light.

The boldness of ʿAmr with the generosity of Hatim, with the forbearance of al-Ahnaf and the intelligence of Iyas.

One of the patron's companions objected to him and said: How do you equate the prince with the boors of the Arabs? The prince is above whom you have described. Abu Tammam, after lowering his head for a moment, replied:

Do not deny my striking an example for him with one lesser than him,

For God has struck the lesser example for His light, a likeness of the niche and the lamp-wick.

Therefore we take care to have a dim light (wasina) at night, for example, to protect our movement from collision.
