Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 39, verse 71:

We notice here that the verb (wa-sīqa, "and they were driven") comes in the passive form, the form for the one whose agent is not named. In another place Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness﴾ [Qaf: 21]. So who is the driver? They said: they are the angels, who drive the people of the Fire to Jahannam, and Allah forbid. The driver (al-sā'iq) is the one who urges the one being driven to hurry, like the rider of a beast who spurs it and urges it so that it hastens with him. Likewise the angels deal with the criminals, urging them toward Jahannam so that they hasten to it.

This shows that the angels are enraged at them, hateful toward them, and offended by their deeds in the world. Therefore they push them toward their just recompense in Jahannam, without leniency and without mercy. Have you seen the police, when they seize a criminal, what do they do to him? They beat him, torture him, and humiliate him, because he is a corrupt member of society whom everyone wants to be rid of. And it is well known that the angels are honoured servants who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and do what they are commanded.

The Qur'an depicts this situation in another verse, where He, glorified be He, says: ﴿On the Day they will be thrust into the Fire of Jahannam with a thrust﴾ [al-Tur: 13]. That is: they will drive them into it and push them into it against their will.

The meaning of (zumaran) is: groups. Everyone who opposes the method of Allah is together in a group: those who abandon the prayer are a group, those who abandon zakat are a group, those who consume usury are a group, and so on. The oppressors, the bribe-takers, the thieves, the adulterers, and the embezzlers: Allah gathers each of them with his companion, and they are gathered together, with their greatest leading them.

Leadership among them is as He said: ﴿The Day We will call every people with their imam..﴾ [al-Isra: 71], and He said: ﴿Then We will surely draw out from every sect whichever of them was most insolent toward the Most Merciful﴾ [Maryam: 69].

And concerning Pharaoh He said: ﴿He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection and bring them down to the Fire, and wretched is the place to which they are brought﴾ [Hud: 98].

That the leaders of misguidance and the heads of disbelief go ahead of their followers indicates the cutting off of the hope of the others for salvation. If the follower enters and does not find his leader, his heart would be attached to him, and he would think that he would come and rescue him. But the reality is that he will enter and find his teacher and exemplar in misguidance has already preceded him to Jahannam.

Until, when they reach its gates, it is opened for them: ﴿until, when they come to it, its gates are opened..﴾ [al-Zumar: 71], because the gate of wrath is not ajar (mish mafannad), rather it is closed and opened only out of necessity, in contrast with the gate of mercy, which is always open. This is from the mercy of Allah, for the mercy of Allah precedes His wrath.

This end to which the people of the Fire come was written for them, and Allah the Truth knew it from the beginning of life. Read, if you wish, His saying, the Exalted: ﴿On the Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission; so among them are the wretched and the blessed. As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire, for them therein is groaning and wailing, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord is the Accomplisher of what He intends. And as for those who were blessed, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills, a gift unbroken﴾ [Hud: 105-108].

First: to understand this verse you must first know the meaning of khulud (abiding). Khulud is a long stay, and this stay is called khulud because it has a beginning but no end. The discussion here concerns those who were blessed, who are the people of Paradise, and those who were wretched, who are the people of the Fire. But Allah the Exalted made an exception for some of these and some of those, and the khulud of those whom Allah excepted will be shortened. How?

The disbeliever, after he is reckoned and driven to Jahannam, its gate is opened for him and he remains abiding in it, a complete abiding from the beginning to no end. Likewise the believer whom the mercy of his Lord overtakes, after he is reckoned, is driven to Paradise, and he remains in it, a complete abiding from the beginning to no end.

As for the exception, it applies to the disobedient believer who did not repent of his sins, or repented but his repentance was not accepted. He must receive the recompense for these sins, and be touched by a lash of the Fire, Allah forbid. This is at the beginning: he enters the Fire for as long as Allah wills, then He brings him out to Paradise. Thus his period of abiding in Paradise is shorter than that of his believing brethren, and the shortening here is from the beginning. Likewise his abiding in the Fire is shorter than that of the eternal people of the Fire.

And His saying: ﴿And its keepers will say to them..﴾ [al-Zumar: 71], that is: the keepers of the Fire said to them, as a rebuke and reproach: ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you the signs of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?..﴾ [al-Zumar: 71]. This interrogation silenced them and left them without argument, for their Lord, mighty and majestic, did not seize them unawares; rather He sent to them messengers. These messengers were "from among you" (minkum), of your kind and of your middle and closest to you, so that the example of them would be easy to follow.

With these messengers were proofs, evidences, promise and threat. Therefore they could not deny: ﴿They will say, "Yes..."﴾ [al-Zumar: 71], that is: this happened. So they confessed against themselves, and the argument was dropped, that Allah had sent to them the messengers who warned them of this day.

So: the warnings that occur to people in their lives are part of the complete mercy of Allah toward creation, and the warnings given earlier in life about what will follow them are part of the complete mercy of Allah toward creation. Have you seen how, when you make your son aware of the consequence of neglect and frighten him of failing at the end of the year, you help him to study and strive so that he does not meet that consequence, and so that he is not surprised by something he neglected?

For this reason the orientalists stopped at surah al-Rahman and said: His saying ﴿He created man from clay like pottery, and He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? He released the two seas, meeting side by side; between them is a barrier they do not transgress. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? From them emerge pearls and coral. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? And to Him belong the ships raised high on the sea like landmarks. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [al-Rahman: 14-25]. They said: yes, these are blessings, and "So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?" fits them. But what blessing is there in His saying: ﴿There will be sent against you both a flame of fire and smoke, and you will not be able to defend yourselves. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [al-Rahman: 35-36].

Yes: warning of evil before it occurs and cautioning against it before its time is a blessing, indeed one of the greatest blessings of Allah upon man, so that he may take precaution against the matter. Threat, warning, insight and fear are only so that we may beware of what is feared, and not fall into it.

As for His saying: ﴿But the word of punishment has come due upon the disbelievers﴾ [al-Zumar: 71], that is: it became obligatory for them despite the warning and the insight. The word that came due is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿"I will surely fill Jahannam with jinn and mankind all together"﴾ [al-Sajdah: 13]. So what are you waiting for after that? What is astonishing is that by our foolish choices we assist destiny, and destiny paves the way for destiny.

The word (kalima) is a single term that conveys only a meaning in itself; it does not convey a predicative meaning. For example, the word "sky" (al-sama') alone does not convey a meaning on which silence is fitting. But when you say "the sky is clear," it gives an understood meaning on which silence is fitting. They said: yet a single word may convey meaning: if you say, "Who is with you?" and one answers, "Zayd," it conveys: "Zayd is with me." Were it not for the supposition of the word "with me," it would not convey anything. Thus the word, then, does not convey a meaning on which silence is fitting except by being combined with another.

The grammarians explained this when they divided the word into noun, verb and particle, and each of these is called a "word" (kalima). The difference between them is that the noun gives in itself a meaning independently understood; the verb gives a meaning in itself, but it is tied to a time or time is part of it. You say: "akala" (he ate), meaning in the past; "ya'kulu" (he eats), in the present; and "kul" (eat!), in the future. As for the particle, it does not give an independently understood meaning; rather it requires a complement to show its meaning.

The word is also used to mean speech. You say: "I delivered a word (kalima) at the gathering," and you mean a sermon. The Qur'an has used the word in this sense in His saying: ﴿By no means! It is merely a word he is saying..﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 100], and the word meant is His saying: ﴿"My Lord, send me back, that I may do righteousness in what I have left behind"..﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 99-100].

Likewise here: ﴿the word of punishment has come due upon the disbelievers﴾ [al-Zumar: 71]; the word is ﴿"I will surely fill Jahannam with jinn and mankind all together"﴾ [al-Sajdah: 13].

... We also note His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Enter the gates of Hell﴾, and He did not say: "Enter Hell." So what is the difference between the two expressions? He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Enter the gates of Hell﴾, because the punishment rushes toward them and hastens to them the moment they enter it; it meets them at its gate.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 39, verse 73:

Here too the angels drive them, but with a difference between the driving of the disbelievers and the driving of the God-fearing. The disbelievers are driven by the angels so that the punishment may be hastened upon them, a driving full of rebuke and harshness. As for the God-fearing, they are driven in the manner of one who loves driving his beloved, so that the bliss may be hastened for them.

His saying (zumaran) means: in groups, each group separate from the others. So these are the ascetics, these are the scholars, these are the warriors, and these are the trustworthy ones. ﴿Until, when they reach it and its gates are opened...﴾ [al-Zumar: 73]. There He said (futihat), and here (wa-futihat). They said of the people of the Fire: (futihat) is the answer of the conditional clause. But here (wa-futihat) is not the answer of the conditional clause; rather, the answer of the conditional clause is the bliss mentioned after it, because the opening of the gates is not the goal, but the goal is what follows it of bliss.

So the waw here is conjunctive, and the clause ﴿and its gates were opened﴾ [al-Zumar: 73] is conjoined to ﴿until, when they reach it﴾ [al-Zumar: 73]. This is because the believers did not doubt this day, whereas the disbelievers doubt it; therefore (futihat abwabuha) [al-Zumar: 71] was made the answer of the conditional clause before it.

As for the God-fearing, the answer of the conditional clause is loftier than the mere opening of the gates for them. These gates open onto the mercy that He will mention afterwards, and mention its components, and how it proceeds, beginning with the angels' greeting to them: ﴿And its keepers will say to them: "Peace be upon you; you have been good, so enter it, abiding therein"﴾ [al-Zumar: 73], because you purified yourselves from the defilement of sins and polytheism, up to the end of the surah, where they see the angels circling around the Throne. This is the answer of the conditional clause that befits them.

Another group of scholars said: the answer of the conditional clause is (wa-futihat), and this waw is the waw of eight (wāw al-thamāniya). What is meant by the waw of eight? They said: the highest count among the Arabs was seven, so when something comes after the seven, they regard it as a new statement and join it with the waw. Among this is the saying of Allah the Exalted about the People of the Cave: ﴿They will say: "They were three, the fourth of them their dog"; and they will say: "They were five, the sixth of them their dog," guessing at the unseen; and they will say: "They were seven, and the eighth of them their dog"﴾ [al-Kahf: 22]. So before the eighth He mentions the waw.

Also among this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿The repentant, the worshippers, the praisers, the wanderers, the bowers, the prostrators, those who enjoin right and forbid wrong, and those who keep the limits of Allah; and give good tidings to the believers﴾ [al-Tawbah: 112]. The word (al-nahunna, "those who forbid") is the eighth, and therefore it was preceded by the waw...

We do not hold this view. The word (wa-futihat) is not the answer of the conditional clause here, because the answer of the conditional clause in regard to the God-fearing is loftier than the opening of the gates for them, and loftier than the angels' saying to them ﴿Peace be upon you﴾ [al-Zumar: 73], and loftier than ﴿you have been good, so enter it, abiding therein﴾ [al-Zumar: 73]. For the Exalted Lord will say afterwards: ﴿And you will see the angels circling around the Throne, glorifying their Lord with His praise﴾ [al-Zumar: 75]. Mentioning the Throne here, with the angels circling it glorifying their Lord with His praise, is an indication of the utmost bliss that the God-fearing will attain, where they will see the Exalted Truth who established Himself upon this Throne. This is the goal that is fitting to be the answer of the preceding conditional clause.

But why did Allah conceal the answer of the conditional clause in this way? They said: because if it had been stated, saying, "in it is what no eye has seen, nor ear has heard, nor has it occurred to the heart of a human," then it would have been heard already. Rather, He, glory be to Him, wished it to be a surprise, in that it is of what does not occur to the heart of a human; that is, it does not come to mind.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 39, verse 74:

Their saying: ﴿And they will say, "Praise be to Allah..."﴾ [al-Zumar: 74]. Is it praise for Allah's truthfulness in the promise, or is it because, by Allah's enabling grace, you believed Allah in what He promised you? The meaning: Praise be to Allah, who made us worthy that His promise be fulfilled concerning us because we affirmed it; otherwise, Allah's promise is true, truly true.

﴿And He has caused us to inherit the earth...﴾ [al-Zumar: 74]. Inheritance here has a meaning other than the one we know, namely that a person inherits from another after his death. The inheritance here is in Paradise, as Allah the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿And they will be called out, "This is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do."﴾ [al-A'raf: 43].

The explanation of this, as we have said, is that Allah, glorified is He, decreed from eternity that He would create creatures, and that He would leave them choice in some matters, and compel them in other matters, so that they remain servants to Him, glorified is He, despite their noses from one aspect, and servants in what they choose from another aspect.

So if they prefer the side of Allah, the Exalted, and prefer His will over what was entrusted to them of choice, they attain the station of servitude to Allah, and at that time they are better than the angels, because the angels were created upon obedience, whereas man was given choice: he obeys or disobeys. If he obeys, he has the right to be proud even over the angels.

Therefore Iblis, before he disobeyed, used to be proud over the angels, and he was called "the peacock of the angels," because he was a chosen creature. Yet he obeyed as the angels obeyed, so he had a distinction over them, until he committed the final slip, and he was cast out and expelled from the mercy of Allah.

We say: When Allah created creatures with choice, that they may obey and that they may disobey, He prepared for them the abode of recompense in Paradise, on the basis that they would all obey, so each one of them has a station in Paradise. Likewise He prepared for them in the Fire places sufficient for all of them if they disobeyed. So when the people of the Fire go to the Fire, their places in Paradise are emptied, so where do they go? The people of Paradise take them, or inherit them, as the Qur'an says.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿We take up residence in Paradise wherever we will...﴾ [al-Zumar: 74]. We say: "Tabawwa'a al-makan" means he settled in the place, and from this is His saying, the Exalted, in the story of Yusuf, peace be upon him: ﴿Thus did We establish Yusuf in the land, to settle therein wherever he willed. We bestow Our mercy upon whom We will﴾ [Yusuf: 56]. The meaning is: we descend and dwell. But the matter is not by force; each goes wherever he wills, and there is in it no transgression upon the rights of others. So the meaning is: we dwell wherever we will, each in his own garden and in what was allotted to him, not in the garden of another, and this is evidence that the garden allotted to him is spacious. ﴿How excellent is the reward of the workers﴾ [al-Zumar: 74]. "Ni'ma" here is for praise, meaning: a great reward that they attained by their righteous deeds.

Regarding His words, ﴿circling around the Throne﴾. It means they go around it, ﴿glorifying their Lord with His praise﴾. So they have no work except glorifying their Lord with praise. ﴿And judgment will be passed between them with truth﴾. That is, Allah judges between them. Between whom? Between the angels, because they are of different ranks. Among them are the *al-'Alun* (the exalted ones), who are absorbed in the Truth, may He be glorified, and who know nothing of our world or of Adam and his offspring.

Among them are those subjected to serving humanity, namely the guardian angels, about whom Allah said: ﴿For him there are successive [angels] before him and behind him, who guard him by the command of Allah﴾ [al-Ra'd: 11]. These are the ones Allah commanded to prostrate to Adam, not all the angels. So this prostration was a sign of submission and obedience to this creature whom you will serve. And among the noble angels are the recorders: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble recorders, who know whatever you do﴾ [al-Infitar: 10-12].

So the meaning of ﴿and judgment will be passed between them with truth﴾ is that each of them takes his rank and the reward he deserves.

﴿And it will be said: All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Zumar: 75]. Who is the speaker? Some said it was said by the believers among mankind. Others said it was said by all creation. Others said it was said by the Truth, may He be glorified, so it is a praise from Allah upon His own Self, may He be glorified, just as He testified for Himself that ﴿there is no deity except Him﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18].

So Allah, may He be glorified, praised Himself for being the Lord of the worlds. Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said in the hadith: "This is a praise from Allah upon Allah. O Allah, make us always among those who say: All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds."
